title.zh: 卷一百五十八 列傳第八十三 韋張嚴韓
title.en: Volume 158 Biographies 83: Wei, Zhang, Yan, Han
title.raw: 卷一百五十八 列傳第八十三 韋張嚴韓 Volume 158 Biographies 83: Wei, Zhang, Yan, Han

sentences.zh: 韋張嚴韓

translations.literal: Wei, Zhang, Yan, Han
translations.idiomatic: Wei, Zhang, Yan, and Han

sentences.zh: 韋臯，字城武，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Gao, style name Chengwu, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao, whose style name was Chengwu, came from Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 六代祖範，有勛力周、隋間。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Fan had meritorious service between the Zhou and Sui dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations back, his ancestor Fan had won distinction in the service of Zhou and Sui.

sentences.zh: 臯始仕為建陵挽郎，諸帥府更辟，擢監察御史。

translations.literal: Gao first took office as a mourning attendant at Jianling; various commanders' headquarters repeatedly recruited him, and he was promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Gao began his career as a mourning attendant at Jianling. After successive appointments in several commanders' staffs, he was promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 張鎰節度鳳翔，署營田判官。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yin was military governor of Fengxiang, he appointed Gao camp-field commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yin served as military governor of Fengxiang, he appointed Gao camp-field commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以殿中侍御史知隴州行營留事。

translations.literal: As palace attendant censor he handled the remaining affairs of the Longzhou field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: As palace attendant censor, he was left in charge of affairs at the Longzhou field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 德宗狩奉天，李楚琳殺鎰，劫眾叛歸朱泚，隴州刺史郝通奔降楚琳。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong was at Fengtian on campaign, Li Chulin killed Yin, seized the troops, and rebelled to join Zhu Ci; Longzhou prefect Hao Tong fled and surrendered to Chulin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong was campaigning at Fengtian, Li Chulin murdered Zhang Yin, seized the army, and defected to Zhu Ci. Longzhou prefect Hao Tong fled and surrendered to Chulin.

sentences.zh: 始，泚以范陽軍鎮鳳翔，既歸節，而留兵五百戍隴上，以部將牛雲光督之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ci had garrisoned Fengxiang with the Fanyang army, after he returned to his command he left five hundred men to guard Long, with his subordinate Niu Yunguang in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhu Ci had stationed the Fanyang army at Fengxiang, he had kept five hundred troops on garrison duty in Long after returning to his command, placing them under his subordinate Niu Yunguang.

sentences.zh: 至是，雲光謀請臯為帥，將劫以臣泚。

translations.literal: At this time Yunguang plotted to make Gao commander and intended to coerce him into submitting to Ci.
translations.idiomatic: At this juncture Yunguang plotted to install Gao as commander and intended to force him to submit to Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 別將翟曄伺知以白臯。

translations.literal: The deputy commander Zhai Ye detected it and informed Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Zhai Ye discovered the plot and reported it to Gao.

sentences.zh: 雲光懼不克，率眾出奔，至汧陽，遇泚奴使臯所，謂雲光曰：「太尉已為天子，使我以御史中丞授臯。

translations.literal: Yunguang, fearing failure, led his men out in flight. At Qianyang he met one of Ci's envoys on his way to Gao, who said to Yunguang: "The Grand Preceptor has already become Son of Heaven and has sent me to invest Gao as vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he would fail, Yunguang led his troops out in flight. At Qianyang he met one of Zhu Ci's envoys bound for Gao, who told him, "The Grand Preceptor has already declared himself emperor and has sent me to appoint Gao vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 若聽，固吾人也，不受，可遂誅之。

translations.literal: If he accepts, he is surely one of us; if not, you may execute him at once.
translations.idiomatic: If he accepts, he is one of us; if not, you may put him to death at once.

sentences.zh: 請以兵俱。

translations.literal: Please bring your troops along.
translations.idiomatic: Bring your troops with you.

sentences.zh: 」許之。

translations.literal: " He agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Yunguang agreed.

sentences.zh: 臯迎勞，先納奴，偽受泚詔。

translations.literal: Gao went out to welcome them with courtesy, first admitting the envoy and falsely accepting Ci's edict.
translations.idiomatic: Gao went out to welcome them courteously, first admitting the envoy and pretending to accept Zhu Ci's edict.

sentences.zh: 即讓雲光曰：「既去而復，何也？

translations.literal: He then reproached Yunguang, saying: "You left and have returned—why?
translations.idiomatic: He then reproached Yunguang: "You left and have come back—why?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「向未知公之命，故去；

translations.literal: " He replied: "Before I did not know your command, so I left;
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Before I did not know your wishes, so I left.

sentences.zh: 今還，願與公同生死。

translations.literal: now I have returned and wish to live and die with you."
translations.idiomatic: Now I have returned and wish to live and die with you."

sentences.zh: 」臯曰：「大使固善，茍無它圖，請釋甲以安眾，而後可入也。

translations.literal: " Gao said: "The envoy is certainly well disposed; if you have no other design, please lay down your armor to reassure the masses, and only then may you enter."
translations.idiomatic: " Gao said, "The envoy is well disposed toward us. If you have no other design, lay down your armor to reassure the troops, and only then may you enter."

sentences.zh: 」雲光以臯諸生，亡能為，乃命士委仗鎧，臯受而內其卒。

translations.literal: " Yunguang, taking Gao for a mere scholar with no ability to act, ordered the soldiers to hand over weapons and armor; Gao received them and admitted the troops within.
translations.idiomatic: " Yunguang, judging Gao a mere scholar incapable of decisive action, ordered his men to surrender their weapons and armor. Gao took them in and admitted the troops within the walls.

sentences.zh: 明日，置酒大會，奴、雲光與其下至，臯伏甲左右廡，酒行，盡殺之，以其首徇。

translations.literal: The next day he held a great banquet; the envoy, Yunguang, and their subordinates all came. Gao had armed men concealed in the side halls on both sides; when the wine was served he had them all killed and displayed their heads as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he held a great banquet. The envoy, Yunguang, and their subordinates all attended. Gao had armed men hidden in the side halls; when the wine was served he had them all killed and displayed their heads as a warning.

sentences.zh: 泚復使它奴拜臯鳳翔節度使，臯亦斬之及從騎三人，縱一人使報泚。

translations.literal: Ci again sent another envoy to invest Gao as military governor of Fengxiang; Gao also beheaded him and three mounted attendants, releasing one man to report back to Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci sent another envoy to invest Gao as military governor of Fengxiang. Gao beheaded him as well, along with three mounted attendants, and let one man go to report back to Ci.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，乃授臯隴州刺史，置奉義軍，拜節度使，寵其功。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he appointed Gao prefect of Longzhou, established the Fengyi Army, and invested him as military governor, honoring his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he appointed Gao prefect of Longzhou, established the Fengyi Army, and made him its military governor, richly rewarding his achievement.

sentences.zh: 臯遣兄平及弇繼至奉天，士氣益壯，乃築壇血牲與士盟曰：「協力一心，以誅元惡，有渝此盟，神其殛之。

translations.literal: Gao sent his elder brother Ping and Yan in succession to Fengtian, and morale grew stronger. He then built an altar, sacrificed a victim with blood, and swore an oath with the troops, saying: "Let us unite in one heart to execute the arch-villain; whoever violates this oath, may the spirits strike him down.
translations.idiomatic: Gao sent his elder brother Ping and Yan in succession to Fengtian, and morale grew stronger. He built an altar, sacrificed a victim, and swore an oath with the troops: "Let us unite as one to execute the arch-villain. Whoever violates this oath, may the spirits strike him down.

sentences.zh: 」又馳使吐蕃與連和，隴坻遂安。

translations.literal: " He also sent swift envoys to ally with the Tibetans, and the Long frontier was thereby secured.
translations.idiomatic: " He also sent swift envoys to ally with Tibet, and the Long frontier was secured.

sentences.zh: 帝自梁、洋還，召為左金吾衛將軍，遷大將軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from Liang and Yang, Gao was summoned as general of the Left Golden Crow Guard and promoted to great general.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from Liang and Yang, Gao was summoned to serve as general of the Left Golden Crow Guard and was promoted to great general.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，代張延賞為劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era he replaced Zhang Yanshang as military governor of Jiannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan era he replaced Zhang Yanshang as military governor of Jiannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 初，雲南蠻羈附吐蕃，其盜塞必以蠻為鄉道。

translations.literal: Previously the Yunnan tribes had been bound to Tibet; whenever they raided the border they always used the tribes as local guides.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Yunnan tribes had been tied to Tibet, and whenever they raided the frontier they always relied on tribal guides.

sentences.zh: 臯計得雲南則斬虜右支，乃間使招徠之，稍稍通西南夷。

translations.literal: Gao calculated that winning Yunnan would cut off the enemy's right wing, so he sent secret envoys to win them over and gradually opened relations with the southwestern tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Gao reckoned that winning Yunnan would sever the enemy's right flank, so he sent secret envoys to win the tribes over and gradually opened contact with the southwestern peoples.

sentences.zh: 明年，蠻大首領苴那時以王爵讓其兄子烏星。

translations.literal: The next year the great tribal leader Ju Nashi yielded his royal title to his elder brother's son Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the great tribal leader Ju Nashi yielded his royal title to his elder brother's son Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 始，烏星幼，那時攝領其部，故請歸爵。

translations.literal: Earlier Wuxing had been young and Nashi had governed the tribe in his stead, so he now asked to return the title.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxing had been young, and Nashi had governed the tribe in his stead, so he now asked to return the title.

sentences.zh: 臯上言：「禮讓行於殊俗，則怫戾者化，願皆封以示褒進。

translations.literal: Gao memorialized: "When courtesy and yielding are practiced even among foreign peoples, the recalcitrant are transformed; I ask that both be enfeoffed to show commendation and advancement."
translations.idiomatic: Gao memorialized the throne: "When courtesy and yielding are practiced even among foreign peoples, the recalcitrant are transformed. I ask that both men be enfeoffed to show commendation and advancement."

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict approved his request.

sentences.zh: 又明年，雲南款邊求內屬，約東蠻鬼主驃傍、苴夢沖等絕吐蕃盟。

translations.literal: The year after that Yunnan came to the border in friendship seeking to submit, agreeing with the eastern tribal spirit-lords Piao Pang, Ju Mengchong, and others to break their alliance with Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that Yunnan came to the frontier in friendship seeking to submit, and agreed with the eastern tribal spirit-lords Piao Pang, Ju Mengchong, and others to break their alliance with Tibet.

sentences.zh: 五年，東蠻斷瀘水橋攻吐蕃，請臯濟師。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the eastern tribes cut the Ludu Bridge and attacked Tibet, requesting that Gao send reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the eastern tribes destroyed the Ludu Bridge and attacked Tibet, asking Gao to send reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 臯遣精卒二千，與蠻共破吐蕃於臺登，殺青海大酋乞臧遮遮、臘城酋悉多楊朱及論東柴等，虜墜死崖谷不可計，多獲牛馬鎧裝。

translations.literal: Gao sent two thousand picked troops, and together with the tribes they defeated Tibet at Taideng, killing the great Qinghai chieftain Qizang Zhezhe, the Lacheng chieftain Siduo Yangzhu, Lun Dongchai, and others; countless enemy soldiers fell to their deaths in cliffs and ravines, and they captured large numbers of cattle, horses, and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Gao sent two thousand picked troops, and together with the tribes they defeated the Tibetans at Taideng, killing the great Qinghai chieftain Qizang Zhezhe, the Lacheng chieftain Siduo Yangzhu, Lun Dongchai, and others. Countless enemy soldiers fell to their deaths in cliffs and ravines, and the victors captured large numbers of cattle, horses, and armor.

sentences.zh: 遮遮，尚結贊之子，虜貴將悍雄者也；

translations.literal: Zhezhe was the son of Shang Jiezan, a noble Tibetan general fierce and formidable;
translations.idiomatic: Zhezhe was the son of Shang Jiezan, a noble Tibetan general renowned for his ferocity;

sentences.zh: 既敗，酋長百餘行哭隨之。

translations.literal: after his defeat more than a hundred chieftains followed in procession weeping.
translations.idiomatic: after his defeat more than a hundred chieftains followed in procession, weeping.

sentences.zh: 悍將已亡，則屯柵以次降定。

translations.literal: Once the fierce generals were gone, the stockaded posts submitted in succession and were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Once the fierce generals were gone, the stockaded posts submitted in succession and were pacified.

sentences.zh: 進檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was advanced to acting minister of civil offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting minister of civil offices.

sentences.zh: 初，東蠻地二千里，勝兵常數萬，南倚閣羅鳳，西結吐蕃，狙勢強弱為患，臯能綏服之，故戰有功。

translations.literal: Previously the eastern tribal lands stretched two thousand li, with tens of thousands of effectives; south they relied on Geluofeng, west they allied with Tibet, and they watched the balance of power to make trouble. Gao was able to pacify them, and therefore his campaigns succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern tribal lands had stretched two thousand li, with tens of thousands of fighting men. To the south they relied on Geluofeng, to the west they allied with Tibet, and they watched the balance of power to make trouble. Gao was able to pacify them, and therefore his campaigns succeeded.

sentences.zh: 詔以那時為順政王、夢沖懷化王、驃傍和義王，刻「兩林」、「勿鄧」等印以賜之。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed Nashi as Prince of Shunzheng, Mengchong as Prince of Huaihua, and Piao Pang as Prince of Heyi, and carved seals reading "Lianglin" and "Wudeng" and the like to bestow on them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict enfeoffed Nashi as Prince of Shunzheng, Mengchong as Prince of Huaihua, and Piao Pang as Prince of Heyi, and had seals reading "Lianglin" and "Wudeng" carved and bestowed on them.

sentences.zh: 而夢沖復與吐蕃盟，臯遣別將蘇峞召之，詰其叛，斬於琵琶川，立次鬼主樣棄等，蠻部震服。

translations.literal: But Mengchong again allied with Tibet; Gao sent the deputy commander Su Wei to summon him, questioned his rebellion, and executed him at Pipaqian, installing the next spirit-lord Yangqi and others, and the tribal divisions were awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: But Mengchong allied with Tibet again. Gao sent deputy commander Su Wei to summon him, questioned his rebellion, and executed him at Pipaqian. He installed the next spirit-lord Yangqi and others, and the tribal divisions were awed into submission.

sentences.zh: 乃建安夷軍於資州，維制諸蠻；

translations.literal: He then established the Anyi Army at Zizhou to restrain the various tribes;
translations.idiomatic: He then established the Anyi Army at Zizhou to restrain the various tribes;

sentences.zh: 城龍溪於西山，保納降羌。

translations.literal: and fortified Longxi in the western mountains to shelter and receive surrendering Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: and fortified Longxi in the western mountains to shelter surrendering Qiang.

sentences.zh: 九年，天子城鹽州，策虜且來橈襲，詔臯出師牽維之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Son of Heaven fortified Yazhou, anticipating that the enemy would come to harass and raid, and ordered Gao to take the field to tie them down.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the emperor fortified Yazhou, anticipating that the enemy would come to harass the frontier, and ordered Gao to take the field to tie them down.

sentences.zh: 乃命大將董勔、張芬分出西山、靈關，破峨和、通鶴、定廉城，逾的博嶺，遂圍維州，搏棲雞，攻下羊溪等三城，取劍山屯焚之。

translations.literal: He then ordered the great generals Dong Kan and Zhang Fen to advance separately from Xishan and Lingguan, capturing Ehe, Tonghe, Dingliancheng, crossing Dibo Ridge, then investing Weizhou, striking Qiji, taking three cities including Yangxi, seizing Jianshan garrison and burning it.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered great generals Dong Kan and Zhang Fen to advance separately from Xishan and Lingguan, capturing Ehe, Tonghe, and Dingliancheng, crossing Dibo Ridge, then investing Weizhou, striking Qiji, taking three cities including Yangxi, and seizing and burning the Jianshan garrison.

sentences.zh: 南道元帥論莽熱來援，與戰，破其軍，進收白岸，乃城鹽州。

translations.literal: The southern-route commander Lun Mangre came to the rescue; they fought and routed his army, advanced to recover Baian, and then fortified Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The southern-route commander Lun Mangre came to the rescue. Gao's forces fought and routed his army, advanced to recover Baian, and then fortified Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 詔臯休士。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Gao to rest the troops.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Gao to stand his troops down.

sentences.zh: 以功為檢校尚書右仆射、扶風縣伯。

translations.literal: For his merit he was made acting right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and Baron of Fufeng County.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made acting right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and Baron of Fufeng County.

sentences.zh: 於是西山羌女、訶陵、南水、白狗、逋租、弱水、清遠、咄霸八國酋長，皆因臯請入朝。

translations.literal: Thereupon the chieftains of the eight western mountain states—Qiangnu, Heling, Nanshui, Baigou, Bozu, Ruoshui, Qingyuan, and Duoba—all requested audience through Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the chieftains of the eight western mountain states—Qiangnu, Heling, Nanshui, Baigou, Bozu, Ruoshui, Qingyuan, and Duoba—all requested audience at court through Gao.

sentences.zh: 乃遣幕府崔佐時由石門趣雲南，而南詔復通。

translations.literal: He then sent his staff member Cui Zuoshi by way of Shimen toward Yunnan, and communication with Nanzhao was restored.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his staff member Cui Zuoshi by way of Shimen toward Yunnan, and communication with Nanzhao was restored.

sentences.zh: 石門者，隋史萬歲南征道也，天寶中，鮮于仲通下兵南溪，道遂閉。

translations.literal: Shimen was the route of Shi Wansui's southern campaign in Sui; in the Tianbao era Xianyu Zhongtong led troops down to Nanxi and the road was thereafter closed.
translations.idiomatic: Shimen was the route of Shi Wansui's southern campaign in Sui. In the Tianbao era Xianyu Zhongtong led troops to Nanxi, and the road was thereafter closed.

sentences.zh: 至是蠻徑北谷，近吐蕃，故臯治復之。

translations.literal: At this time the tribal route passed through the northern valley close to Tibet, so Gao restored it.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the tribal route passed through the northern valley close to Tibet, so Gao restored it.

sentences.zh: 繇黎州出邛部，直雲南，置青溪關，號曰「南道」。

translations.literal: From Lizhou it went out through Qiongbu straight to Yunnan; he established Qingxi Pass and called it the "Southern Route."
translations.idiomatic: From Lizhou it ran out through Qiongbu straight to Yunnan. He established Qingxi Pass and called it the "Southern Route."

sentences.zh: 乃詔臯統押近界諸蠻、西山八國、雲南安撫使。

translations.literal: An edict then placed Gao in overall charge of the nearby tribes, the eight western mountain states, and the Yunnan pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then placed Gao in overall charge of the nearby tribes, the eight western mountain states, and the Yunnan pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 俄進同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was advanced to honorary co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he was advanced to honorary co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 十三年，復巂州。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he recovered Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he recovered Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃怨，完壘造舟謀擾邊，臯輒破卻之。

translations.literal: Tibet resented this, repaired fortifications and built boats planning to harass the border, but Gao repeatedly defeated and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet resented this, repaired fortifications and built boats planning to harass the frontier, but Gao repeatedly defeated and repelled them.

sentences.zh: 自是曩貢、臘城等九節度嬰嬰、籠官馬定德與大將舉落皆降，昆明管些蠻又內附。

translations.literal: From this time the nine military commissioners of Nangong, Lacheng, and the like—Yingying, the cage-official Ma Dingde, and the great general Juluo—all submitted, and the Guanxi tribes of Kunming also came within.
translations.idiomatic: From this time the nine military commissioners of Nangong, Lacheng, and the like—Yingying, the cage-official Ma Dingde, and the great general Juluo—all submitted, and the Guanxi tribes of Kunming also came within.

sentences.zh: 贊普怒，遂北掠靈、朔，破麟州以取償焉。

translations.literal: The tsenpo was enraged and thereupon raided north into Ling and Shuo, capturing Linzhou to take compensation.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan emperor was enraged and raided north into Ling and Shuo, capturing Linzhou to exact compensation.

sentences.zh: 帝詔臯深入以橈虜。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Gao to penetrate deeply to harass the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Gao to penetrate deeply and harass the enemy.

sentences.zh: 臯遣大將陳泊等出三奇，崔堯臣趨石門無衣山，仇冕、董振走維州，邢玼出黃崖略棲雞、老翁城，高倜、王英俊繇峨和、清溪道薄故松州，元膺出濕山、成溪，臧守至道黎、巂，韋良金趨平夷，路惟明自靈關、夏陽攻逋租、偏松城，王有道涉大度河，陳孝陽率蠻苴那時等道西瀘攻昆明、諾濟，師無慮五萬，以八月悉出塞。

translations.literal: Gao sent the great general Chen Bo and others out through Sanqi, Cui Yaochan toward Shimen and Wuyishan, Qiu Mian and Dong Zhen toward Weizhou, Xing Qi out from Huangya to strike Qiji and Laowengcheng, Gao Tong and Wang Yingjun by the Ehe and Qingxi routes to press old Songzhou, Yuan Ying out through Shishan and Chengxi, Zang Shouzhi by way of Li and Xi, Wei Liangjin toward Pingyi, Lu Weiming from Lingguan and Xiayang to attack Bozu and Piansongcheng, Wang Youdao crossing the Dadu River, Chen Xiaoyang leading the tribes under Ju Nashi by the western Lu route to attack Kunming and Nuoji—forces numbering no less than fifty thousand, all going out beyond the passes in the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: Gao sent great general Chen Bo and others out through Sanqi, Cui Yaochan toward Shimen and Wuyishan, Qiu Mian and Dong Zhen toward Weizhou, Xing Qi from Huangya to strike Qiji and Laowengcheng, Gao Tong and Wang Yingjun by the Ehe and Qingxi routes to press old Songzhou, Yuan Ying through Shishan and Chengxi, Zang Shouzhi by way of Li and Xi, Wei Liangjin toward Pingyi, Lu Weiming from Lingguan and Xiayang to attack Bozu and Piansongcheng, Wang Youdao crossing the Dadu River, and Chen Xiaoyang leading the tribes under Ju Nashi by the western Lu route to attack Kunming and Nuoji. The army numbered no less than fifty thousand men, and in the eighth month they all marched out beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 十月，大破吐蕃，拔其保鎮捕候，追奔轉戰千里，遂圍維州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month they inflicted a great defeat on Tibet, capturing their fortified posts and outposts, pursuing the fleeing enemy in battle over a thousand li, and then investing Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they inflicted a great defeat on the Tibetans, capturing their fortified posts and outposts, pursuing the fleeing enemy in battle for a thousand li, and then investing Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃釋靈、朔兵，使論莽熱以內大相兼東境五節度大使，率雜虜十萬來救。

translations.literal: Tibet released its troops from Ling and Shuo and sent Lun Mangre, as inner chief minister and concurrently eastern frontier commissioner over five circuits, leading a hundred thousand mixed barbarian troops to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet released its troops from Ling and Shuo and sent Lun Mangre, serving as inner chief minister and concurrently as eastern frontier commissioner over five circuits, leading a hundred thousand mixed barbarian troops to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 師伏以待，虜乘勝深入，師噪而奮，虜大潰，生禽莽熱獻諸朝。

translations.literal: The army lay in ambush awaiting them; the enemy, riding their victory, pressed deep in, whereupon the army shouted and charged, the enemy collapsed in great disorder, and Mangre was captured alive and presented to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The army lay in ambush. The enemy, emboldened by their earlier success, pressed deep in, whereupon Gao's troops shouted and charged. The enemy collapsed in great disorder, and Mangre was captured alive and presented to the court.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，進檢校司徒兼中書令、南康郡王，帝制紀功碑褒賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and advanced him to acting grand mentor concurrently director of the Secretariat, Prince of Nankang Commandery; the emperor himself composed a merit stele to praise and reward him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and advanced him to acting grand mentor concurrently director of the Secretariat and Prince of Nankang Commandery. The emperor himself composed a merit stele to praise and reward him.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，詔檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong acceded, an edict appointed him acting grand preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong acceded, an edict appointed him acting grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 會王叔文等幹政，臯遣劉辟來京師謁叔文曰：「公使私於君，請盡領劍南，則惟君之報。

translations.literal: When Wang Shuwen and others seized power, Gao sent Liu Pi to the capital to call on Shuwen, saying: "Your envoy has come to you in private: if you grant full command of Jiannan, then you shall have only my gratitude in return.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shuwen and others seized power, Gao sent Liu Pi to the capital to visit Shuwen, saying, "I have sent my envoy to you in private: if you grant me full command of Jiannan, you shall have only my gratitude in return.

sentences.zh: 不然，惟君之怨。

translations.literal: Otherwise, only my resentment toward you."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, you shall have only my resentment."

sentences.zh: 」叔文怒，欲斬辟，辟遁去。

translations.literal: " Shuwen was enraged and wished to execute Pi, but Pi fled.
translations.idiomatic: " Shuwen was enraged and wished to execute Pi, but Pi fled.

sentences.zh: 臯知叔文多釁，又自以大臣可與國大議，即上表請皇太子監國，又上箋太子，暴叔文、伾之奸，且勸進。

translations.literal: Gao knew that Shuwen had many causes for grievance, and also considered himself a senior minister fit to deliberate on great affairs of state; he thereupon submitted a memorial asking that the crown prince supervise the state, and also sent a letter to the crown prince exposing the treachery of Shuwen and Yi and urging him to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Gao knew that Shuwen had many enemies, and considered himself a senior minister fit to deliberate on great affairs of state. He submitted a memorial asking that the crown prince supervise the state, and also sent a letter to the crown prince exposing the treachery of Shuwen and Yi and urging him to advance.

sentences.zh: 會大臣繼請，太子遂受禪，因投殛奸黨。

translations.literal: As senior ministers followed with repeated requests, the crown prince thereupon received the abdication and thereby executed the treacherous faction.
translations.idiomatic: As senior ministers followed with repeated requests, the crown prince received the abdication and had the treacherous faction executed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，臯暴卒，年六十一，贈太師，謚曰忠武。

translations.literal: That year Gao died suddenly at the age of sixty-one; he was posthumously made grand preceptor and given the posthumous title Zhongwu, "Loyal and Martial."
translations.idiomatic: That year Gao died suddenly at the age of sixty-one. He was posthumously made grand preceptor and given the posthumous title Zhongwu, "Loyal and Martial."

sentences.zh: 臯治蜀二十一年，數出師，凡破吐蕃四十八萬，禽殺節度、都督、城主、籠官千五百，斬首五萬餘級，獲牛羊二十五萬，收器械六百三十萬，其功烈為西南劇。

translations.literal: Gao governed Shu for twenty-one years and took the field many times; in all he defeated four hundred eighty thousand Tibetans, captured or killed fifteen hundred military commissioners, protectors, city lords, and cage-officials, took more than fifty thousand heads, seized two hundred fifty thousand cattle and sheep, and recovered six million three hundred thousand pieces of equipment—his achievements were the greatest in the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Gao governed Shu for twenty-one years and took the field many times. In all he defeated four hundred eighty thousand Tibetans, captured or killed fifteen hundred military commissioners, protectors, city lords, and cage-officials, took more than fifty thousand heads, seized two hundred fifty thousand cattle and sheep, and recovered six million three hundred thousand pieces of equipment. His achievements were the greatest in the southwest.

sentences.zh: 善拊士，至雖昏嫁皆厚資之，婿給錦衣，女給銀塗衣，賜各萬錢，死喪者稱是。

translations.literal: He was skilled at comforting troops; even weddings and funerals were richly subsidized—sons-in-law were given brocade robes, daughters silvered garments, each received ten thousand cash in gifts, and the dead were treated likewise.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at winning over his troops. Even weddings and funerals were richly subsidized: sons-in-law received brocade robes, daughters silvered garments, each family received ten thousand cash in gifts, and the dead were treated with equal generosity.

sentences.zh: 其僚掾官雖顯，不使還朝，即署屬州刺史，自以侈橫，務蓋藏之。

translations.literal: Even when his staff officials grew prominent he would not let them return to court, but immediately appointed them prefects of subordinate prefectures; he was extravagant and overbearing himself and strove to conceal his wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Even when his staff officials grew prominent he would not let them return to court, but immediately appointed them prefects of subordinate prefectures. He was extravagant and overbearing himself and strove to conceal his wealth.

sentences.zh: 故劉辟階其厲，卒以叛。

translations.literal: Therefore Liu Pi followed his example and in the end rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi followed his example and in the end rebelled.

sentences.zh: 朝廷欲追繩其咎，而不與臯者詆所進兵皆鏤「定秦」字，有陸暢者上言：「臣向在蜀，知『定秦』者，匠名也。

translations.literal: The court wished to pursue his faults in accountability, but those unfriendly to Gao slandered him, saying the weapons he presented were all engraved with the characters "Ding Qin." Lu Chang memorialized: "When I was formerly in Shu I knew that 'Ding Qin' was a craftsman's name."
translations.idiomatic: The court wished to hold him accountable, but his enemies slandered him, saying the weapons he had presented were all engraved with the characters "Ding Qin." Lu Chang memorialized: "When I was in Shu I knew that 'Ding Qin' was a craftsman's name."

sentences.zh: 」繇是議息。

translations.literal: " Thereby the inquiry ceased.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereby the inquiry ceased.

sentences.zh: 暢，字達夫，臯雅所厚禮。

translations.literal: Chang, style name Dafu, was one whom Gao had always treated with generous courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, whose style name was Dafu, was one whom Gao had always treated with generous courtesy.

sentences.zh: 始，天寶時，李白為《蜀道難》篇以斥嚴武，暢更為《蜀道易》以美臯焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Tianbao era Li Bai had written "The Road to Shu Is Hard" to criticize Yan Wu; Chang rewrote it as "The Road to Shu Is Easy" to praise Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Tianbao era Li Bai had written "The Road to Shu Is Hard" to criticize Yan Wu. Chang rewrote it as "The Road to Shu Is Easy" to praise Gao.

sentences.zh: 始，臯務私其民，列州互除租，凡三歲一復。

translations.literal: From the beginning Gao sought to favor his people; the prefectures in turn remitted taxes, with a general remission every three years.
translations.idiomatic: From the beginning Gao sought to favor his people. The prefectures in turn remitted taxes, with a general remission every three years.

sentences.zh: 臯沒，蜀人德之，見其遺象必拜。

translations.literal: After Gao's death the people of Shu honored him; whenever they saw his portrait they would bow.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao's death the people of Shu honored him. Whenever they saw his portrait they bowed.

sentences.zh: 凡刻石著臯名者，皆镵其文尊諱之。

translations.literal: Wherever stone was carved bearing Gao's name, the text was chiseled away in observance of naming taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever stone was carved bearing Gao's name, the text was chiseled away in observance of naming taboo.

sentences.zh: 兄聿，弟平。

translations.literal: His elder brother was Yu; his younger brother was Ping.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother was Yu; his younger brother was Ping.

sentences.zh: 聿以蔭調南陵尉，遷秘書郎，以父嫌名換太子司議郎，辟淮南杜佑府。

translations.literal: Yu entered office by yin privilege as aide of Nanling, was transferred to secretary, and because of his father's taboo name was exchanged to crown prince secretary for memorials; he was recruited into Du You's Huainan staff.
translations.idiomatic: Yu entered office by yin privilege as aide of Nanling, was transferred to secretary, and because of his father's taboo name was reassigned as crown prince secretary for memorials. He was recruited into Du You's Huainan staff.

sentences.zh: 元和初，為國子司業。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era he became vice director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe era he became vice director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 劉辟與盧文若反，臯子行式娶文若女弟，聿不以聞。

translations.literal: When Liu Pi and Lu Wenruo rebelled, Gao's son Xingshi had married Wenruo's younger sister, but Yu did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Pi and Lu Wenruo rebelled, Gao's son Xingshi had married Wenruo's younger sister, but Yu did not report it.

sentences.zh: 辟平，行式妻當沒掖庭，有司並按聿，或以道遠不應坐，乃皆赦之。

translations.literal: When the rebellion was pacified, Xingshi's wife was to be sent to the palace women; the authorities jointly prosecuted Yu, but some held that because of the distance he should not be punished, and all were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was pacified, Xingshi's wife was to be sent to the palace women. The authorities prosecuted Yu as well, but some held that because of the distance he should not be punished, and all were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 終太子右庶子。

translations.literal: He ended as right vice guardian of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as right vice guardian of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 平與臯斬朱泚使者，間走奉天上功，擢萬年尉。

translations.literal: Ping, together with Gao, beheaded Zhu Ci's envoys and made his way secretly to Fengtian to report merit; he was promoted to aide of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: Ping, together with Gao, beheaded Zhu Ci's envoys and made his way secretly to Fengtian to report his merit. He was promoted to aide of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 平子正貫，字公理，少孤，臯謂能大其門，名曰臧孫。

translations.literal: Ping's son Zhengguan, style name Gongli, was orphaned young; Gao said he could enlarge the clan gate and called him Zangsun.
translations.idiomatic: Ping's son Zhengguan, whose style name was Gongli, was orphaned young. Gao said he could enlarge the clan and called him Zangsun.

sentences.zh: 推蔭為單父尉，不得意，棄官去，改今名。

translations.literal: He entered by yin privilege as aide of Shanfu, was dissatisfied, abandoned his post and left, and changed to his present name.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office by yin privilege as aide of Shanfu, was dissatisfied, abandoned his post, and changed to his present name.

sentences.zh: 舉賢良方正異等，除太子校書郎，調華原尉。

translations.literal: He was recommended as outstanding in the erudite and upright category, appointed crown prince collator, and transferred to aide of Huayuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as outstanding in the erudite and upright category, appointed crown prince collator, and transferred to aide of Huayuan.

sentences.zh: 後又中詳閑吏治科，遷萬年主簿，擢累司農卿。

translations.literal: Later he also passed the detailed and familiar with governance category, was transferred to registrar of Wannian, and was promoted in succession to minister of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also passed the examination in detailed knowledge of governance, was transferred to registrar of Wannian, and was promoted in succession to minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 坐尚食乏供，貶均州刺史。

translations.literal: He was demoted to prefect of Junzhou for a failure in the palace commissary's provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to prefect of Junzhou for a failure in the palace commissary's provisions.

sentences.zh: 久之，進壽州團練使。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was advanced to training commissioner of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was advanced to training commissioner of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣宗立，以治當最，拜京兆尹、同州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong acceded, because his governance ranked highest he was appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong acceded, because his governance ranked highest he was appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄擢嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was advanced to military governor of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he was advanced to military governor of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 南海舶賈始至，大帥必取象犀明珠，上珍而售以下直。

translations.literal: When merchant ships first arrived from the Southern Sea, the regional commander always took ivory, rhinoceros horn, and luminous pearls, rating the finest goods and selling them at lower prices.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever merchant ships first arrived from the Southern Seas, the regional commander always seized ivory, rhinoceros horn, and luminous pearls—keeping the finest goods for himself and selling the rest at cut-rate prices.

sentences.zh: 正貫既至，無所取，吏咨其清。

translations.literal: When Zhengguan arrived, he took nothing; officials praised his probity.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengguan arrived, he took nothing from them, and his staff praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 南方風俗右鬼，正貫毀淫祠，教民毋妄祈。

translations.literal: In the south custom honored ghosts; Zhengguan destroyed illicit shrines and taught the people not to pray recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the south set great store by spirits; Zhengguan demolished illicit shrines and taught the people not to pray recklessly.

sentences.zh: 會海水溢，人爭咎撤祠事，以為神不厭，正貫登城沃酒以誓曰：「不當神意，長人任其咎，無逮下民。

translations.literal: It happened that seawater overflowed; people all blamed the destruction of the shrines, thinking the spirits were displeased; Zhengguan ascended the wall, poured libation wine, and vowed: "If this does not accord with the spirits' intent, let the chief bear the blame—do not involve the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Then the sea overflowed. People blamed the destruction of the shrines, saying the spirits were displeased. Zhengguan climbed the city wall, poured a libation of wine, and swore: "If this does not accord with the spirits' will, let the chief bear the blame—not the common people.

sentences.zh: 」俄而水去，民乃信之。

translations.literal: " Before long the water receded, and the people then believed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long the waters receded, and the people believed him.

sentences.zh: 居鎮三歲，既病，遺令無厚葬，無用鼓吹，無請謚。

translations.literal: After three years in the post he fell ill, and left instructions for no lavish burial, no use of musical escort, and no petition for a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in the command he fell ill and left instructions for no lavish burial, no funeral procession with drums and pipes, and no petition for a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十八，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-eight, and was posthumously made minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-eight and was posthumously appointed minister of works.

sentences.zh: 劉辟者，字太初，擢進士宏詞科，佐韋臯府，遷累御史中丞、支度副使。

translations.literal: Liu Pi, style name Taichu, passed the jinshi and Hongci examinations, served in Wei Gao's office, and was transferred in succession to vice censor-in-chief and deputy fiscal commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi, whose style name was Taichu, passed the jinshi and Hongci examinations, served on Wei Gao's staff, and rose in succession to vice censor-in-chief and deputy fiscal commissioner.

sentences.zh: 臯卒，辟主後務，諷諸將僥旄節，憲宗以給事中召之，不奉詔。

translations.literal: When Gao died, Pi took charge of the aftermath, subtly urging the generals to hope for the pennant and staff; Emperor Xianzong summoned him as palace adviser, but he did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao died, Pi took charge of affairs, covertly urging the generals to seek the banner and staff of command. Emperor Xianzong summoned him as a palace adviser, but he refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 時帝新即位，欲靜鎮四方，即拜檢校工部尚書、劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had newly acceded and wished to pacify the regions on all sides, so he immediately appointed him acting minister of works and military governor of Jiannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had only recently acceded and wished to pacify the realm. He promptly appointed Pi acting minister of works and military governor of Jiannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 辟意帝可動，益驁蹇，吐不臣語，求統三川，欲以所善盧文若節度東川，即以兵取梓州。

translations.literal: Pi thought the emperor could be swayed, grew ever more arrogant and obstinate, uttered disloyal words, sought to rule all three river valleys, wished to appoint his favorite Lu Wenruo military governor of East River Circuit, and intended to take Zizhou by force.
translations.idiomatic: Pi thought the emperor could be moved and grew ever more arrogant. He spoke treasonously, sought to rule all three river valleys, and planned to install his favorite Lu Wenruo as military governor of East River Circuit, then use troops to seize Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 且以術家言五福、太一舍於蜀，乃造大樓以祈祥。

translations.literal: Moreover, on the word of diviners that the Five Fortunes and Grand Unity would lodge in Shu, he built a great tower to pray for blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, on the advice of diviners that the Five Fortunes and Grand Unity would lodge in Shu, he built a great tower to pray for auspicious signs.

sentences.zh: 帝始重征討，而宰相杜黃裳勸帝，且言：「辟，妄書生耳，可鼓而俘也。

translations.literal: The emperor began to take punitive action seriously; the chief minister Du Huangshang urged him and said: "Pi is but a foolish scholar—one can rouse troops and capture him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor began to treat the campaign in earnest. Chief Minister Du Huangshang urged him on and said, "Pi is nothing but a foolish scholar. A drumbeat is all it would take to capture him."

sentences.zh: 」薦高崇文、李元弈等將神策行營兵皆西，使嚴礪、李康掎角之。

translations.literal: " He recommended Gao Chongwen and Li Yuanyi and others to lead the Shence field-army troops west, and had Yan Li and Li Kang pinch from two sides.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Gao Chongwen, Li Yuanyi, and others to lead the Shence field-army troops west, with Yan Li and Li Kang coordinating a pincer movement.

sentences.zh: 詔許自新，辟不聽。

translations.literal: An edict permitted him to reform; Pi would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: An edict offered him a chance to submit; Pi refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 崇文取東川，帝乃下詔奪其官，進破鹿頭關，遂下成都。

translations.literal: Chongwen took East River Circuit; the emperor then issued an edict stripping Pi of his offices, advanced and broke through Lutou Pass, and then took Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwen seized East River Circuit. The emperor then issued an edict stripping Pi of his offices. Chongwen advanced, broke through Lutou Pass, and took Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 辟從數十騎走，至羊灌田，自投水，不能死，騎將酈定進禽之。

translations.literal: Pi fled with several dozen horsemen; reaching Yangguan Field, he threw himself into the water but could not die; the cavalry officer Li Ding captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Pi fled with several dozen horsemen. At Yangguan Field he threw himself into the water but failed to drown; cavalry officer Li Ding seized him.

sentences.zh: 文若先殺其族，縋石自沈於江，失其屍。

translations.literal: Wenruo first killed his clan, lowered a stone to sink himself in the river, and his corpse was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Wenruo first executed his own clan, then lowered a stone and sank himself in the river; his body was never recovered.

sentences.zh: 檻車送辟京師，尚冀不死，食飲於道晏然。

translations.literal: Pi was sent to the capital in a caged cart; he still hoped not to die and ate and drank calmly along the way.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was sent to the capital in a caged cart. He still hoped to live and ate and drank along the road with perfect composure.

sentences.zh: 將至都，神策以兵迎之，系其首，曳而入，驚曰：「何至是邪？

translations.literal: As they were about to reach the capital, Shence troops came to meet him; they bound his head and dragged him in; startled, he said: "How did it come to this?
translations.idiomatic: As they neared the capital, Shence troops came to meet them. They bound his head and dragged him in. Startled, he cried, "How did it come to this?"

sentences.zh: 」帝禦興安樓受俘，詔詰反狀，辟曰：「臣不敢反，五院子弟為惡，不能制。

translations.literal: " The emperor ascended Xing'an Tower to receive the captive and ordered an inquiry into the rebellion; Pi said: "Your subject did not dare rebel—the Five Yard youths did evil and I could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ascended Xing'an Tower to receive the captive and ordered an inquiry into the rebellion. Pi said, "Your subject did not dare rebel—the men of the Five Yard did evil, and I could not control them."

sentences.zh: 」詔問：「遣使賜節何不受？

translations.literal: " An edict asked: "When an envoy was sent bearing the banner and staff, why did you not accept?
translations.idiomatic: The edict asked, "When we sent an envoy bearing the banner and staff, why did you not accept?"

sentences.zh: 」乃伏罪。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he acknowledged his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he confessed his guilt.

sentences.zh: 獻廟社，徇於市，斬於城西南獨柳下。

translations.literal: He was offered to the altars of soil and grain, paraded through the market, and executed beneath the Lone Willow southwest of the city.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered to the altars of soil and grain, paraded through the market, and beheaded beneath the Lone Willow southwest of the city.

sentences.zh: 子超郎等九人，與部將崔綱以次誅。

translations.literal: His sons Chao, Lang, and eight others, together with the staff general Cui Gang, were executed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Chao and Lang and seven others, together with staff general Cui Gang, were executed one after another.

sentences.zh: 始，辟嘗病，見問疾者必以手行入其口，辟即裂食之。

translations.literal: At first, when Pi was ill, whenever visitors came to ask after his health he would put his hand into their mouths; Pi would then tear and eat it.
translations.idiomatic: It was said that when Pi was ill, any visitor who came to inquire after his health would find Pi reach into his mouth with his own hand—and then tear off the flesh and eat it.

sentences.zh: 唯盧文若至，如平常，故益與之厚，而皆夷族。

translations.literal: Only when Lu Wenruo came was it as usual; therefore he all the more favored Wenruo, yet all were exterminated to the last clan member.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Lu Wenruo visited did he behave as usual; Pi therefore grew all the closer to him—yet in the end they were all exterminated to the last clan member.

sentences.zh: 張建封，字本立，鄧州南陽人，客隱兗州。

translations.literal: Zhang Jianfeng, style name Benli, was a native of Nanyang in Dengzhou who lived as a guest-recluse in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianfeng, whose style name was Benli, came from Nanyang in Dengzhou but lived as a guest-recluse in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 父玠，少任俠。

translations.literal: His father Jie was chivalrous and daring in youth.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jie had been chivalrous and bold in his youth.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，使李廷偉脅徇山東，魯郡太守韓擇木迎館之。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he sent Li Tingwei to coerce and subdue the east of the mountains; Han Zhemu, prefect of Lu Prefecture, received and lodged him.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, he sent Li Tingwei to coerce the east of the mountains into submission. Han Zhemu, prefect of Lu Prefecture, received Tingwei and lodged him.

sentences.zh: 玠率豪桀段絳等集兵，將斬以徇，擇木不許，唯司兵參軍張孚助其謀，乃殺廷偉並其黨以聞。

translations.literal: Jie led stalwarts such as Duan Jiang to gather troops, intending to behead Tingwei and display him as warning; Zhemu did not permit it, but only the military aide Zhang Fu helped his plan; then they killed Tingwei and his faction and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Jie led stalwarts such as Duan Jiang to gather troops and intended to behead Tingwei and display him as a warning. Zhemu refused, but military aide Zhang Fu backed the plan. They then killed Tingwei and his followers and reported what they had done.

sentences.zh: 擇木、孚皆受賞，而玠去之江南，不自言功。

translations.literal: Zhemu and Fu both received rewards, but Jie departed for the Jiangnan region and did not himself speak of his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhemu and Fu both received rewards, but Jie went south to the Yangzi region and never spoke of his own merit.

sentences.zh: 建封少喜文章，能辯論，慷慨尚氣，自許以功名顯。

translations.literal: In youth Jianfeng loved literary composition, could debate, was magnanimous and valued spirit, and promised himself renown through meritorious achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Jianfeng loved literature and excelled in debate. He was generous and spirited, and promised himself renown through meritorious achievement.

sentences.zh: 李光弼鎮河南，盜起蘇、常間，殘掠鄉縣。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi governed Henan; bandits rose between Suzhou and Changzhou and ravaged the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi governed Henan. Bandits rose between Suzhou and Changzhou and ravaged the districts and villages.

sentences.zh: 代宗詔中人馬日新與光弼麾下皆討。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong ordered the eunuch Ma Rixin and all under Guangbi to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong ordered the eunuch Ma Rixin and all of Guangbi's subordinates to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 建封見中人，請前喻賊，可不須戰。

translations.literal: Jianfeng met the eunuch and requested to go ahead and persuade the bandits, saying battle might not be needed.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng met the eunuch and asked to go ahead and persuade the bandits, saying bloodshed might be avoided.

sentences.zh: 因到賊屯開譬禍福，一日降數千人，縱還田裏，由是知名。

translations.literal: He therefore went to the bandit encampment and expounded on fortune and misfortune; in one day several thousand surrendered; he released them to return to their fields, and thereby became known.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the bandit encampment and spoke to them of fortune and ruin. In one day several thousand surrendered; he released them to return to their fields, and thereby made his name.

sentences.zh: 湖南觀察使韋之晉辟署參謀，授左清道兵曹參軍，不樂職，輒去。

translations.literal: The Hunan observation commissioner Wei Zhijin recruited him as strategist and appointed him left aide of the Pure Way corps; he did not enjoy the post and left at once.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan observation commissioner Wei Zhijin recruited him as strategist and appointed him left aide of the Pure Way corps, but he did not enjoy the post and left at once.

sentences.zh: 令狐彰節度滑亳，奏置幕府，彰不朝覲，建封非之。

translations.literal: Linghu Zhang governed Hua and Bo and memorialized to establish a staff office; Zhang did not attend court audience; Jianfeng disapproved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Zhang governed Hua and Bo and memorialized to establish a staff office, but Zhang did not come to court. Jianfeng disapproved.

sentences.zh: 往見轉運使劉晏，晏奏試大理評事，使筦漕務，歲餘罷。

translations.literal: He went to see transport commissioner Liu Yan; Yan memorialized to appoint him on probation as recorder of the Court of Judicial Review and had him manage transport affairs; after more than a year he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He went to see transport commissioner Liu Yan, who memorialized to appoint him on probation as recorder of the Court of Judicial Review and had him manage transport affairs. After more than a year he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 時馬燧為三城鎮遏使，雅知之，表為判官，擢監察御史。

translations.literal: At that time Ma Sui was suppressing commissioner of the Three Forts and greatly knew his talent; he memorialized to appoint him as staff judge and promoted him to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ma Sui was suppressing commissioner of the Three Forts and held him in high regard. Sui memorialized to appoint him as staff judge and promoted him to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 燧伐李靈耀，軍中事多所諏訪，從鎮河東，授侍御史，即表其能於朝。

translations.literal: When Sui campaigned against Li Lingyao, he consulted Jianfeng on many military matters; following Sui to govern Hedong, he was appointed attendant censor and Sui at once memorialized on his ability to the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui campaigned against Li Lingyao, he consulted Jianfeng on many military matters. Following Sui to govern Hedong, Jianfeng was appointed attendant censor, and Sui at once memorialized on his abilities to the court.

sentences.zh: 楊炎將任以要職，盧杞不喜，出為岳州刺史。

translations.literal: Yang Yan was about to appoint him to an important post, but Lu Qi disliked him and had him sent out as prefect of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan was about to appoint him to an important post, but Lu Qi disliked him and had him transferred out as prefect of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 李希烈既破梁崇義，跋扈不臣，壽州刺史崔昭與相聞，德宗召宰相選代昭者，杞倉卒不暇取它吏，即白用建封。

translations.literal: After Li Xilie had defeated Liang Chongyi, he was overbearing and disloyal; Cui Zhao, prefect of Shouzhou, communicated with him; Emperor Dezong summoned the chief ministers to choose a replacement for Zhao; Qi in haste had no time to select another official and at once reported to use Jianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Xilie defeated Liang Chongyi, he grew arrogant and disloyal. Cui Zhao, prefect of Shouzhou, was in communication with him. Emperor Dezong summoned the chief ministers to choose Zhao's replacement. Qi, in haste, had no time to select another official and immediately recommended Jianfeng.

sentences.zh: 希烈數敗王師，張甚，遂僭即天子位，淮南節度使陳少遊陰附之。

translations.literal: Xilie repeatedly defeated the imperial armies and grew ever bolder; he then presumptuously assumed the title of Son of Heaven; Chen Shaoyou, military governor of Huainan, secretly attached himself to Xilie.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie repeatedly defeated the imperial armies and grew ever bolder. He then presumptuously declared himself emperor. Chen Shaoyou, military governor of Huainan, secretly sided with him.

sentences.zh: 希烈遣將楊豐賫偽赦二，畀建封、少遊。

translations.literal: Xilie sent the general Yang Feng bearing two false amnesties to present to Jianfeng and Shaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie sent the general Yang Feng bearing two forged amnesties to present to Jianfeng and Shaoyou.

sentences.zh: 豐至，建封縛致軍中，會中人來，對之斬其首，因送偽書於行在。

translations.literal: When Feng arrived, Jianfeng bound him and brought him to the army; when an eunuch envoy came, Jianfeng beheaded Feng in his presence and sent the forged documents to the temporary palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng arrived, Jianfeng bound him and brought him into camp. When an eunuch envoy came, Jianfeng beheaded Feng before him and sent the forged documents to the emperor's temporary residence.

sentences.zh: 少遊聞之，恚汗不自處，建封乃劾其附賊狀，帝方蒙難，不暇治也。

translations.literal: When Shaoyou heard of this, he was enraged and sweated, unable to compose himself; Jianfeng then impeached him for attaching to the rebel; the emperor was then in distress and had no leisure to pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyou heard of this, he was enraged and broke into a sweat, unable to compose himself. Jianfeng then impeached him for siding with the rebel, but the emperor was then in distress and had no leisure to pursue it.

sentences.zh: 希烈又署杜少誠為淮南節度使，約破壽州，以趣江都。

translations.literal: Xilie also appointed Du Shaoqing military governor of Huainan, arranging to take Shouzhou and press on toward Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie also appointed Du Shaoqing military governor of Huainan, planning to seize Shouzhou and push on toward Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 建封壁霍丘秋柵拒之，賊不能東。

translations.literal: Jianfeng fortified himself at the Qiuchai barrier in Huoqiu to resist; the rebels could not advance east.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng fortified himself at the Qiuchai barrier in Huoqiu to resist them, and the rebels could not advance eastward.

sentences.zh: 遷團練使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to training commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to training commissioner.

sentences.zh: 帝還自梁，少遊卒憂死。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from Liang, Shaoyou died of grief and anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from Liang, Shaoyou died of grief and anxiety.

sentences.zh: 進兼御史大夫、濠壽廬觀察使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to concurrent chief censor and observation commissioner of Hao, Shou, and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to concurrent chief censor and observation commissioner of Hao, Shou, and Lu.

sentences.zh: 是時，四方尚多故，乃繕陴隍，益治兵，四鄙附悅。

translations.literal: At that time disturbances still abounded on all sides; he therefore repaired walls and moats, further trained troops, and the people on all four borders were pleased and attached.
translations.idiomatic: At that time disturbances still abounded on all sides. He repaired walls and moats, further trained his troops, and the people on all four borders were pleased and loyal.

sentences.zh: 希烈使票帥悍卒來戰，建封皆沮衄之。

translations.literal: Xilie sent swift-riding brave troops to fight; Jianfeng repulsed and frustrated them all.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie sent swift-riding shock troops to fight him; Jianfeng repulsed them every time.

sentences.zh: 賊平，進封階，又任一子正員官。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was advanced in noble rank and one son was appointed to a regular office.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified, he was advanced in noble rank and one of his sons was appointed to a regular office.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年，拜御史大夫、徐泗濠節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan he was appointed chief censor and military governor of Xu, Si, and Hao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan he was appointed chief censor and military governor of Xu, Si, and Hao.

sentences.zh: 始，李洧以徐降，洧卒，高承宗、獨孤華代之，地迫於寇，常困不支。

translations.literal: At first Li Wei surrendered Xuzhou; when Wei died, Gao Chengzong and Dugu Hua succeeded him; the territory pressed by rebels was often strained and unable to hold.
translations.idiomatic: At first Li Wei had surrendered Xuzhou. When Wei died, Gao Chengzong and Dugu Hua succeeded him, but the territory, pressed by rebels, was often strained beyond endurance.

sentences.zh: 於是李泌建言：「東南漕自淮達諸汴，徐之埇橋為江、淮計口，今徐州刺史高明應甚少，脫為李納所並，以梗餉路，是失江、淮也。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li Bi offered counsel: "Southeast transport from the Huai reaches the Bian region; Yongqiao in Xu is the chokepoint of the Jiang-Huai route; now the Xu prefect Gao Mingying has few troops; if he should be swallowed by Li Na and the supply route blocked, the Jiang-Huai region would be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Li Bi offered counsel: "Southeast grain transport from the Huai reaches the Bian region. Yongqiao in Xu is the chokepoint of the Jiang-Huai route. The Xu prefect Gao Mingying has few troops; if he should be swallowed by Li Na and the supply route blocked, we would lose the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 請以建封代之，益與濠、泗二州。

translations.literal: I request that Jianfeng replace him and additionally grant the two prefectures of Hao and Si.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Jianfeng replace him and be given the two prefectures of Hao and Si as well."

sentences.zh: 夫徐地重而兵勁，若帥又賢，即淄青震矣。

translations.literal: Xu territory is weighty and its troops strong; if the commander is also worthy, then Zi-Qing would be shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Xu is a vital territory with strong troops. If its commander is also worthy, Zi-Qing would be shaken."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「善。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Good.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 」繇是徐復為雄鎮。

translations.literal: " From this Xu again became a formidable command.
translations.idiomatic: From this Xu again became a formidable command.

sentences.zh: 久之，檢校尚書右仆射。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was made acting right vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was made acting right vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十三年，來朝，帝不待日召見延英殿，詔會朝赴大夫班，以示殊寵，建封賦《朝天行》以獻。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he came to court; the emperor, not waiting for the appointed day, summoned him to audience in Yanying Hall, ordered him to attend court assembly in the chief-minister rank to show special favor, and Jianfeng composed "Song of Attending Court" and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he came to court. The emperor, not waiting for the appointed day, summoned him to audience in Yanying Hall, ordered him to attend court assembly in the chief-minister rank to show special favor, and Jianfeng composed "Song of Attending Court" and presented it.

sentences.zh: 帝眷遇異等，賜名馬珍具。

translations.literal: The emperor favored him with exceptional regard and bestowed famed horses and rare goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored him with exceptional regard and bestowed famed horses and rare treasures.

sentences.zh: 是時，宦者主宮市，置數十百人閱物廛左，謂之「白望」。

translations.literal: At that time eunuchs controlled the palace market; they posted several dozen to several hundred men to inspect goods by the shopfronts, calling them "white watchers."
translations.idiomatic: At that time eunuchs controlled the palace market. They posted dozens or even hundreds of men to inspect goods by the shopfronts, calling them "white watchers."

sentences.zh: 無詔文驗核，但稱宮市，則莫敢誰何，大率與直十不償一。

translations.literal: Without edict documents for verification, if they merely called it palace market no one dared resist; generally they paid scarcely one part in ten of fair value.
translations.idiomatic: Without edict documents for verification, if they merely invoked the palace market no one dared resist. As a rule they paid scarcely one-tenth of fair value.

sentences.zh: 又邀閽闥所奉及腳傭，至有重荷趨肆而徒返者。

translations.literal: They also intercepted what was carried in tribute at the palace gate and porters' fees; some who bore heavy loads hurried to the market only to return empty-handed.
translations.idiomatic: They also intercepted what was carried in tribute at the palace gate and porters' fees. Some who bore heavy loads hurried to the market only to return empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 有農賣一驢薪，宦人以數尺帛易之，又取它費，且驅驢入宮，而農納薪辭帛，欲亟去，不許，恚曰：「惟有死耳！

translations.literal: A farmer sold a load of firewood carried by a donkey; a eunuch exchanged a few feet of cloth for it, also took other fees, and drove the donkey into the palace; the farmer handed over the firewood and refused the cloth, wishing to leave quickly; they did not permit it; enraged he said: "Only death remains!
translations.idiomatic: A farmer sold a load of firewood carried by a donkey. A eunuch exchanged a few feet of cloth for it, took other fees besides, and drove the donkey into the palace. The farmer handed over the firewood and refused the cloth, wishing to leave at once. When they would not let him go, he cried in rage, "I might as well die!"

sentences.zh: 」遂擊宦者。

translations.literal: " Then he struck the eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: Then he struck the eunuch.

sentences.zh: 有司執之以聞，帝黜宦人，賜農帛十匹，然宮市不廢也。

translations.literal: The authorities seized him and reported; the emperor dismissed the eunuch and bestowed ten bolts of cloth on the farmer, yet the palace market was not abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities seized him and reported the matter. The emperor dismissed the eunuch and bestowed ten bolts of cloth on the farmer, yet the palace market was not abolished.

sentences.zh: 諫臣交章列上，皆不納，故建封請間為帝言之，帝頗順聽。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials submitted memorial after memorial; all were not accepted; therefore Jianfeng requested a private audience to speak to the emperor, and the emperor listened with some accord.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials submitted memorial after memorial, but none was accepted. Jianfeng therefore requested a private audience to speak to the emperor, and the emperor listened with some accord.

sentences.zh: 會詔書蠲民逋賦，帝問何如，答曰：「殘逋積負，決無可斂，雖蠲除之，百姓尚無所益。

translations.literal: It happened that an edict remitted the people's arrears in taxes; the emperor asked what Jianfeng thought; he answered: "Arrears accumulated over years can in no case be collected; even if remitted, the common people would still gain little.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that an edict remitted the people's tax arrears. The emperor asked what Jianfeng thought. He answered, "Arrears accumulated over years can in no case be collected. Even if remitted, the common people would still gain little.

sentences.zh: 」又陳：「河東節度使李說、華州刺史盧征皆病不能事，左右得以為奸。

translations.literal: " He also stated: "Li Shuo, military governor of Hedong, and Lu Zheng, prefect of Hua, are both ill and unable to conduct affairs; those around them are able to do wrong.
translations.idiomatic: He also stated, "Li Shuo, military governor of Hedong, and Lu Zheng, prefect of Hua, are both ill and unable to conduct affairs. Those around them are free to do wrong.

sentences.zh: 右金吾大將軍李翰好刺細事規寵，人疾惡之。

translations.literal: Li Han, right general of the Golden Crow Guard, likes to pry into petty matters to seek favor; people detest him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han, right general of the Golden Crow Guard, likes to pry into petty matters to seek favor, and people detest him."

sentences.zh: 」帝悉嘉可。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of this.

sentences.zh: 未幾，制詔：「官師過從，人情之常，自今金吾勿以聞。」

translations.literal: Before long an imperial decree stated: "Social visiting among officials and teachers is human custom; from now the Golden Crow Guard is not to report it."
translations.idiomatic: Before long an imperial decree stated, "Social visiting among officials and teachers is human custom. From now on the Golden Crow Guard is not to report it."

sentences.zh: 元巳，賜宴曲江，特詔與宰相同榻食。

translations.literal: On the Yuanxi festival, a banquet was granted at Qujiang; a special edict had him dine at the same couch as the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On the Yuanxi festival, a banquet was granted at Qujiang. A special edict had him dine at the same couch as the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 其還鎮，帝賦詩以餞，於時雖馬燧、渾瑊、劉玄佐、李抱真等勛寵卓越，未有以詩餞者。

translations.literal: When he returned to his command, the emperor composed a poem to see him off; although at that time Ma Sui, Hun Zai, Liu Xuanzuo, Li Baozhen, and others had outstanding merit and favor, none had been sent off with a poem.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to his command, the emperor composed a poem to see him off. Although at that time Ma Sui, Hun Zai, Liu Xuanzuo, Li Baozhen, and others had won outstanding merit and favor, none had ever been sent off with a poem.

sentences.zh: 帝又使左右以所持鞭賜之，曰：「卿節誼歲寒弗渝，故用此為況。

translations.literal: The emperor also had attendants bestow the whip he held, saying: "Your constancy and integrity do not change in the cold season; therefore I use this as a symbol.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also had attendants bestow the whip he held, saying, "Your constancy and integrity do not change in the cold season. I give you this as a symbol of that."

sentences.zh: 」建封又賦詩以自警勵。

translations.literal: " Jianfeng also composed a poem to admonish and encourage himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng also composed a poem to admonish and encourage himself.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以病求代，詔韋夏卿代之，未至而建封卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, sick, he requested a replacement; an edict had Wei Xiaqing replace him; before Xiaqing arrived, Jianfeng died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he fell ill and requested a replacement. An edict appointed Wei Xiaqing to replace him, but before Xiaqing arrived, Jianfeng died.

sentences.zh: 年六十六，冊贈司徒。

translations.literal: He was sixty-six; he was canonically posthumously made grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-six. He was canonically posthumously appointed grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 治徐凡十年，躬於所事，一軍大治。

translations.literal: He governed Xu for ten years in all, personally attending to his duties; the whole army was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Xu for ten years in all, personally attending to his duties, and the whole army was brought to excellent order.

sentences.zh: 善容人過，至健黠亦未嘗曲法假之。

translations.literal: He was good at tolerating others' faults, yet even the bold and cunning he never bent the law to indulge.
translations.idiomatic: He was good at tolerating others' faults, yet even the bold and cunning he never bent the law to indulge.

sentences.zh: 其言忠義感激，故下皆畏悅。

translations.literal: His words of loyalty and righteousness were stirring; therefore subordinates both feared and delighted in him.
translations.idiomatic: His words of loyalty and righteousness were stirring, and his subordinates both feared and delighted in him.

sentences.zh: 性樂士，賢不肖遊其門者禮必均，故其往如歸。

translations.literal: By nature he delighted in scholars; whether worthy or unworthy, those who came to his gate received equal courtesy; therefore they came as if returning home.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he delighted in scholars. Whether worthy or unworthy, those who came to his gate received equal courtesy, and they came as if returning home.

sentences.zh: 許孟容、韓愈皆奏署幕府，有文章傳於時。

translations.literal: Xu Mengrong and Han Yu were both memorialized for staff appointment; their writings circulated at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Mengrong and Han Yu were both recruited to his staff. Their writings circulated widely at the time.

sentences.zh: 子愔，始以蔭補虢州參軍事。

translations.literal: His son Yin at first entered by yin privilege as aide in Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin at first entered office by yin privilege as aide in Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建封卒，府佐鄭通誠者攝留事，畏其軍亂，因浙西戍兵過徐，謀引以為援。

translations.literal: When Jianfeng died, the staff assistant Zheng Tongcheng acted as acting commander; fearing the army would riot, as the Zhexi garrison troops passed through Xu he plotted to bring them in as support.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianfeng died, staff assistant Zheng Tongcheng acted as acting commander. Fearing the army would riot, and noting that Zhexi garrison troops were passing through Xu, he plotted to bring them in as support.

sentences.zh: 舉軍怒，斧庫取兵，環府大噪，殺通誠及大將數人，乃表於朝，請愔為留後，假旄節。

translations.literal: The whole army was enraged; they broke the armory with axes and seized weapons, surrounded the headquarters with great clamor, killed Tongcheng and several great generals, then memorialized the court requesting Yin as acting commander with temporary banner and staff.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army was enraged. They broke into the armory with axes and seized weapons, surrounded headquarters with a great clamor, killed Tongcheng and several senior generals, and then memorialized the court requesting Yin as acting commander with temporary banner and staff.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，披濠、泗隸淮南，詔杜佑討徐亂。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it; he stripped Hao and Si and attached them to Huainan, and ordered Du You to suppress the Xu unrest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused. He stripped Hao and Si from Xu and attached them to Huainan, and ordered Du You to suppress the unrest in Xu.

sentences.zh: 泗州刺史張伾以兵攻埇橋，與徐軍遇，伾大敗。

translations.literal: Zhang Pei, prefect of Sizhou, attacked Yongqiao with troops; he met the Xu army and Pei was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pei, prefect of Sizhou, attacked Yongqiao with troops. He met the Xu army and was utterly defeated.

sentences.zh: 帝未有以制，乃授愔右驍衛將軍、徐州刺史，知留後。

translations.literal: The emperor had no means to control them; he therefore appointed Yin right general of the Valiant Cavalry Guard and Xu prefect, acting commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no means to control them. He therefore appointed Yin right general of the Valiant Cavalry Guard and prefect of Xu, acting commander.

sentences.zh: 以伾為泗州留後，杜兼為濠州留後。

translations.literal: Pei was made acting commander of Sizhou; Du Jian was made acting commander of Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pei was made acting commander of Sizhou, and Du Jian was made acting commander of Hao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俄進愔武寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Yin was advanced to military governor of the Wuning Army.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter Yin was advanced to military governor of the Wuning Army.

sentences.zh: 元和初，以疾求代，召為工部尚書，以王紹節度武寧，還濠、泗隸徐。

translations.literal: At the start of the Yuanhe era, sick, he requested a replacement; he was summoned as minister of works; Wang Shao was made military governor of Wuning and Hao and Si were restored to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanhe era he fell ill and requested a replacement. He was summoned as minister of works. Wang Shao was made military governor of Wuning, and Hao and Si were restored to Xu's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 徐人喜，遂不敢亂，而愔得行。

translations.literal: The people of Xu rejoiced and then did not dare riot; Yin was able to depart.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Xu rejoiced and did not dare riot again. Yin was able to depart.

sentences.zh: 未逾境，卒。

translations.literal: Before he had crossed the border he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had crossed the border he died.

sentences.zh: 愔治徐七年，其政稱治。

translations.literal: Yin governed Xu for seven years; his administration was praised as well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yin governed Xuzhou for seven years, and his rule was widely regarded as a model of good governance.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書右仆射。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 嚴震，字遐聞，梓州鹽亭人。

translations.literal: Yan Zhen, courtesy name Xianwen, was a native of Yanting in Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhen, styled Xianwen, came from Yanting in Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 本農家子，以財役裏閭。

translations.literal: He was originally a farmer's son who used his wealth to command the neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: Born to a farming family, he used his wealth to dominate local affairs in his district.

sentences.zh: 至德、乾元中，數出資助邊，得為州長史。

translations.literal: During the Zhide and Qianyuan eras, he repeatedly contributed funds to support the frontier and was appointed long-term secretary of a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhide and Qianyuan reigns he made repeated donations to support border defense, earning appointment as a prefectural long-term secretary.

sentences.zh: 西川節度使嚴武知其才，署押衙，遷恒王府司馬，委以軍府眾務。

translations.literal: The military governor of Xichuan, Yan Wu, recognizing his talent, appointed him yamen adjutant, then promoted him to Secretary of the Prince of Heng's household, entrusting him with all military headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wu, military governor of Xichuan, recognized his ability and made him yamen adjutant, then promoted him to secretary of the Prince of Heng's household, putting him in charge of the command's daily business.

sentences.zh: 武卒，罷歸。

translations.literal: When Wu died, he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan Wu's death, he left office and went home.

sentences.zh: 會東川節度使李叔明表為渝州刺史，震以叔明姻家，移疾去。

translations.literal: Soon the military governor of Dongchuan, Li Shuming, recommended him as Prefect of Yuzhou, but Zhen, being related to Li Shuming by marriage, resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shuming, military governor of Dongchuan, recommended him for the prefecture of Yuzhou, Zhen declined on grounds of illness because Li was a relation by marriage.

sentences.zh: 山南西道節度府又表為鳳州刺史。

translations.literal: The military headquarters of Shannan West Circuit again recommended him as Prefect of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Shannan West headquarters then recommended him to govern Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 母喪解。

translations.literal: He resigned upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 起為興、鳳兩州團練使，好興利除害。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed Rectification and Training Commissioner of Xing and Feng Prefectures; he loved to promote profit and eliminate harm.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to serve as Rectification and Training Commissioner for Xing and Feng, he devoted himself to public benefit and the removal of abuses.

sentences.zh: 建中中，劍南黜陟使韋楨狀震治行為山南第一，乃賜上下考，封鄖國公。

translations.literal: In the Jianzhong era, the inspection commissioner for Jiannan, Wei Zhen, reported Zhen's administrative conduct as first in Shannan; he was then given top evaluation grades and enfeoffed as Duke of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianzhong, Wei Zhen, the Jiannan inspection commissioner, ranked Zhen's governance first in all Shannan; the court awarded him the highest merit ratings and enfeoffed him as Duke of Yun.

sentences.zh: 治鳳十四年，號稱清嚴，遠邇咨美。

translations.literal: He governed Feng for fourteen years, renowned for severity and rectitude, praised near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Over fourteen years at Fengzhou his rule was known for its austerity and integrity, winning praise throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 遷山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military governor of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to military governor of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 朱泚反，遣腹心穆廷光等遺帛書誘之，震即斬以聞。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he sent his trusted men Mu Tingguang and others with a letter on silk to entice him; Zhen immediately beheaded them and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rose in rebellion, he sent trusted agents including Mu Tingguang with a silk letter to win Zhen over; Zhen had them executed at once and reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 是時，李懷光與賊連和，奉天危蹙，帝欲徙蹕山南，震聞，馳表奉迎，遣大將張用誠以兵五千扞衛。

translations.literal: At this time Li Huaiguang allied with the rebels; Fengtian was in dire peril and the emperor wished to move the imperial seat to Shannan. On hearing this, Zhen urgently submitted a memorial offering welcome and sent the great general Zhang Yongcheng with five thousand troops to protect and escort.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang had joined the rebels, Fengtian was in grave danger, and the emperor planned to move the court into Shannan. Zhen immediately memorialized offering a loyal welcome and dispatched his senior general Zhang Yongcheng with five thousand men to guard the route.

sentences.zh: 用誠至盩厔有反計，帝憂之，會震牙將馬勛嗣至，帝告以故，勛曰：「臣請歸取節度符召之，即不受，斬其首以復命。

translations.literal: When Yongcheng reached Zhouzhi he harbored plans to rebel; the emperor was worried.
