As it happened Ma Xun, Zhen's garrison general, arrived; the emperor told him the reason, and Xun said: "Your servant requests to go back, take the military governor's tally and summon him; if he does not obey, I will cut off his head and return to report."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongcheng reached Zhouzhi with treason in mind, and the emperor grew anxious. Ma Xun, a staff general under Zhen, happened to arrive at court; when the emperor explained the situation, Xun said, "Let me return for the governor's tally and summon him. If he refuses, I will bring back his head."

sentences.zh: 」帝悅，使計日往。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and had him set out within a few days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and ordered him to depart within the agreed number of days.

sentences.zh: 勛還得符，請壯士五人與偕，出駱谷，用誠以為未知其謀，以數百騎迓勛館之，左右嚴侍。

translations.literal: Xun returned and obtained the tally; he requested five stout warriors to accompany him and set out through Luogu Pass. Yongcheng, not knowing his plan, met Xun with several hundred cavalry and lodged him, with attendants standing guard strictly on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xun returned with the tally, took five strong men with him, and went out through Luogu Pass. Zhang Yongcheng, unaware of the plot, greeted him with several hundred horsemen, put him up at an inn, and posted guards on every side.

sentences.zh: 勛未發，陰令焚草館外，士寒爭附火，勛從容引符示之，曰：「大夫召君。

translations.literal: Before Xun set out, he secretly had grass burned outside the lodge; the soldiers, cold, scrambled to huddle around the fire. Xun calmly produced the tally and showed it, saying: "The Grandee summons you."
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving, Xun secretly ordered a fire lit outside the lodge. The cold soldiers crowded around the flames, and Xun calmly produced the governor's tally and said, "The governor summons you."

sentences.zh: 」用誠懼，將走，壯士自後禽之。

translations.literal: Yongcheng was afraid and about to flee; the stout warriors seized him from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongcheng panicked and tried to run, but the strongmen grabbed him from behind.

sentences.zh: 用誠子斫勛傷首，左右扞刀得免，遂仆用誠，而格殺其子。

translations.literal: Yongcheng's son hacked at Xun and wounded his head; those at Xun's side parried the blade and he escaped injury; he then threw Yongcheng down and killed his son in the struggle.
translations.idiomatic: Yongcheng's son struck at Xun and cut his head, but Xun's attendants blocked the blow. Xun then threw Yongcheng to the ground and killed the son in the scuffle.

sentences.zh: 勛即軍中，士皆擐甲矣。

translations.literal: Xun went immediately into the army camp; the soldiers had all already put on armor.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xun went straight into the camp and found the men already armored.

sentences.zh: 勛昌言曰：「若父母妻子在梁州，今棄之而反，何所利邪？

translations.literal: Xun addressed them openly, saying: "Your parents, wives, and children are in Liangzhou; if you now abandon them and rebel, what advantage is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xun spoke plainly to the troops: "Your parents, wives, and children are in Liangzhou. What good will it do you to abandon them and rebel?"

sentences.zh: 大夫取用誠爾，若等無與！

translations.literal: The Grandee wanted only Yongcheng; you have nothing to do with it!
translations.idiomatic: The governor seeks only Yongcheng—this has nothing to do with the rest of you!

sentences.zh: 」眾乃服，不敢動。

translations.literal: The crowd then submitted and did not dare stir.
translations.idiomatic: The men submitted and did not dare move.

sentences.zh: 即縛用誠送於震，杖殺之，而拔其副以統師。

translations.literal: He immediately bound Yongcheng and sent him to Zhen, who had him beaten to death, then promoted his deputy to command the army.
translations.idiomatic: He bound Zhang Yongcheng and sent him to Yan Zhen, who had him beaten to death, then promoted the deputy to take command of the force.

sentences.zh: 始，勛赴行在，逾半日期，帝頗憂。

translations.literal: At first, when Xun was going to the temporary imperial residence, half a day had passed beyond the set date and the emperor was rather worried.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Xun first set out for the temporary court, the deadline passed by half a day and the emperor grew anxious.

sentences.zh: 比至，大喜。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When he finally arrived, the emperor was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 翌日，發奉天。

translations.literal: The next day they departed from Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: The following day the court left Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 既入駱谷，懷光以騎追襲，賴山南兵以免。

translations.literal: After entering Luogu Pass, Huaiguang pursued with cavalry; they were spared harm thanks to the Shannan troops.
translations.idiomatic: Once they entered Luogu Pass, Li Huaiguang pursued with cavalry, but the Shannan troops fought them off and the emperor escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 尋加檢校戶部尚書、馮翊郡王，實封二百戶。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed acting Minister of Revenue and Prince of Fengyi Commandery, with an actual fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting Minister of Revenue and Prince of Fengyi, with a substantive fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 天子至梁州，宰相以為地貧無所仰給，請進幸成都。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven reached Liangzhou, the chief ministers thought the land was poor and provided nothing to rely on for supplies, and requested that he advance to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Liangzhou, the chief ministers argued that the region was too poor to sustain the court and urged him to move on to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 震曰：「山南密邇畿輔，李晟銳於收復，方藉六師為聲援，今引而西，則諸將顧望，責功無期。

translations.literal: Zhen said: "Shannan lies close to the capital region; Li Sheng is eager for recovery and is relying on the imperial army as a supporting force. If we now lead it westward, the various generals will hesitate and look back, and the demand for results will be without end."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen replied, "Shannan lies close to the capital. Li Sheng is pressing hard to recover the realm and needs the imperial army as his rear support. If the court withdraws farther west, the generals will lose heart and victory will never come."

sentences.zh: 」帝未決，會晟表至，亦請駐蹕梁、洋，議遂定。

translations.literal: The emperor had not yet decided when Li Sheng's memorial arrived, also requesting that the imperial carriage halt at Liang and Yang; the decision was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Before the emperor could decide, Li Sheng's memorial arrived urging him to remain at Liang and Yang, and the matter was settled.

sentences.zh: 然梁、漢間刀耕火耨，民采穭為食，雖領十五郡，而賦入才比東方數大縣。

translations.literal: Yet between Liang and Han the people farmed by slash-and-burn; they gathered wild grain for food. Although he governed fifteen prefectures, tax revenue amounted only to that of a few large eastern counties.
translations.idiomatic: Yet between Liangzhou and Hanzhong the people still practiced slash-and-burn farming and lived on wild grain. Though Zhen governed fifteen prefectures, his tax revenue matched only a few large counties in the east.

sentences.zh: 自安、史後，山賊剽掠，戶口流散，震隨宜勸課，鳩斂有法，民不煩擾，而行在供億具焉。

translations.literal: Since the An-Shi Rebellion, mountain bandits had plundered and households had scattered. Zhen as suited the circumstances encouraged cultivation and taxation; his collection had method, the people were not troubled, and supplies for the temporary imperial residence were all provided.
translations.idiomatic: Since the An Lushan rebellion, bandits had ravaged the hills and the population had fled. Zhen adapted his policies to local conditions, levied taxes in an orderly way without harassing the people, and fully supplied the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 車駕將還，加檢校尚書左仆射。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was about to return, he was additionally appointed acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to return to the capital, Zhen was made acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 詔改梁州為興元府，即用震為尹，加實封二百戶。

translations.literal: An edict changed Liangzhou to Xingyuan Prefecture; Zhen was immediately made its governor and granted an additional actual fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: An edict renamed Liangzhou as Xingyuan Prefecture and appointed Zhen its governor, adding two hundred households to his substantive fief.

sentences.zh: 久之，進同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: After some time, he was promoted to co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was promoted to co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 貞元十五年卒，年七十六，贈太保，謚曰忠穆。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan he died at age seventy-six; he was posthumously given Grand Mentor and the posthumous title Zhongmu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan at the age of seventy-six. The court posthumously appointed him Grand Mentor and gave him the posthumous name Loyal and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 從孫譔，與宰相楊收善。

translations.literal: His grand-nephew Tan was on good terms with the Chief Minister Yang Shou.
translations.idiomatic: His grand-nephew Yan Tan was a close associate of Chief Minister Yang Shou.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，繇桂管觀察使擢為江西節度使，改號鎮南軍。

translations.literal: In the Xiantong era, from Guangxi Observing Commissioner he was promoted to military governor of Jiangxi; the circuit name was changed to Zhennan Army.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiantong he rose from Guangxi Observing Commissioner to military governor of Jiangxi, and the circuit was renamed the Zhennan Army.

sentences.zh: 時南蠻內寇，詔譔募士三萬備之。

translations.literal: At that time the southern barbarians invaded the interior; an edict ordered Tan to recruit thirty thousand soldiers to prepare against them.
translations.idiomatic: When southern tribes raided the interior, the court ordered Tan to raise thirty thousand men for defense.

sentences.zh: 或言譔廣補卒，擅納縑廩。

translations.literal: Some said Tan broadly supplemented troops and on his own authority collected silk and grain provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Reports circulated that Tan had over-recruited soldiers and illegally collected silk and grain rations.

sentences.zh: 及收得罪，韋保衡以譔素善收，賕賄狼藉，遣使按覆，詔賜死。

translations.literal: When Shou was convicted of a crime, Wei Baoheng, because Tan had long been friendly with Shou and his bribery was flagrant, sent envoys to investigate; an edict ordered him to die by grace.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Shou fell from power, Wei Baoheng cited Tan's long friendship with Shou and his rampant corruption, sent investigators, and secured an edict ordering Tan to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 韓弘，滑州匡城人。

translations.literal: Han Hong, a native of Kuangcheng in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong came from Kuangcheng in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，依其舅劉玄佐。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he relied on his maternal uncle Liu Xuanzuo.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father early and was raised under his maternal uncle Liu Xuanzuo.

sentences.zh: 舉明經不中，從外家學騎射。

translations.literal: He failed the Mingjing examination and learned mounted archery from his mother's family.
translations.idiomatic: After failing the Mingjing civil examination, he trained in horsemanship and archery in his uncle's household.

sentences.zh: 由諸曹試大理評事，為宋州南城將。

translations.literal: Through various office trials he became an assistant director in the Court of Judicial Review and served as garrison commander of Nancheng in Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service through routine office trials, became an assistant director in the Court of Judicial Review, and was posted as garrison commander at Nancheng in Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 事劉全諒，署都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Serving Liu Quanliang, he was appointed director of all military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Quanliang he was appointed director of all military affairs.

sentences.zh: 貞元十五年，全諒死，軍中思玄佐，以弘才武，共立為留後，請監軍表諸朝。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan, when Quanliang died, the army missed Xuanzuo; because Hong had talent and martial skill, they jointly installed him as acting governor and requested the army supervisor report it to the court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan, after Quanliang died, the troops longed for Liu Xuanzuo's leadership. Impressed by Hong's ability and martial prowess, they installed him as acting governor and had the army supervisor report the appointment to court.

sentences.zh: 詔檢校工部尚書，充宣武節度副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him acting Minister of Works, as vice military governor of Xuanwu, managing circuit affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed him acting Minister of Works and vice military governor of Xuanwu, with full charge of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 先是，曲環死，吳少誠與全諒謀襲陳許，使數輩仍在館。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qu Huan died, Wu Shaoqian and Quanliang plotted to raid Chen and Xu; they sent several men who remained lodged there.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Qu Huan's death, Wu Shaoqian and Quanliang plotted a strike against Chen and Xu and kept several envoys lodged at the post station.

sentences.zh: 弘始得帥，欲以忠自表於眾，即驅出少誠使斬之，選卒三千，會諸軍擊少誠，敗之。

translations.literal: When Hong first obtained command, wishing to demonstrate loyalty to the crowd, he immediately drove out Shaoqian's envoys and had them beheaded; he selected three thousand soldiers, joined the various armies to attack Shaoqian, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Hong took command he sought to prove his loyalty: he expelled Wu Shaoqian's envoys and had them executed, then picked three thousand men, joined the allied armies, and routed Shaoqian.

sentences.zh: 汴自劉士寧以來，軍益驕，及殺陸長源，主帥勢輕，不可制。

translations.literal: Bian since Liu Shining had become increasingly arrogant; after they killed Lu Changyuan, commanders held less authority and could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liu Shining's day the Bianzhou army had grown ever more insubordinate, and after the murder of Lu Changyuan its commanders wielded too little authority to restrain the troops.

sentences.zh: 弘察軍中素恣橫者劉鍔等三百人，一日，數其罪斬之牙門，流血丹道，弘言笑自如。

translations.literal: Hong identified three hundred men in the army who had long been willful and violent, such as Liu E; one day he enumerated their crimes and executed them at headquarters gate; blood flowed across the red path, yet Hong spoke and laughed as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Hong singled out three hundred habitual ruffians in the ranks, including Liu E. One day he read out their crimes and executed them at headquarters; blood ran deep across the courtyard, yet Hong spoke and laughed as calmly as ever.

sentences.zh: 自是訖弘去，無一敢肆者。

translations.literal: From then until Hong departed, not one dared to act willfully.
translations.idiomatic: From that day until Hong left office, not a single soldier dared to run wild.

sentences.zh: 李師古屯曹州，以謀鄭、滑，或告：「師古治道矣，兵且至，請備之。

translations.literal: Li Shigu was encamped at Caozhou, scheming against Zheng and Hua; someone reported: "Shigu is repairing the roads; troops will soon arrive—please prepare."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shigu was encamped at Caozhou with designs on Zheng and Hua, when someone warned, "Shigu is repairing the roads—his army will arrive soon. We must prepare."

sentences.zh: 」弘曰：「師來不除道也。

translations.literal: Hong said: "When troops come they do not repair the roads."
translations.idiomatic: Hong replied, "Armies on the march do not repair roads beforehand."

sentences.zh: 」師古情得，乃引去。

translations.literal: Shigu's intentions were discovered and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Realizing his plan was exposed, Shigu withdrew.

sentences.zh: 累授檢校司空、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed acting Minister of Works and co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively made acting Minister of Works and co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 弘以官與太原王鍔等，詒書宰相，恥為鍔下。

translations.literal: Hong, holding the same rank as Wang E of Taiyuan and others, wrote to the chief ministers complaining that he was ashamed to rank below E.
translations.idiomatic: Hong held the same rank as Wang E of Taiyuan and others, and wrote the chief ministers that he was ashamed to stand below E in precedence.

sentences.zh: 憲宗方用兵淮西，藉其重，更授檢校司徒，班鍔上。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong was then deploying troops in Huai West and relied on Hong's weight; he was further appointed acting Grand Mentor and ranked above E.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong was campaigning in Huai West and needed Hong's prestige; he was therefore made acting Grand Mentor and given precedence over Wang E.

sentences.zh: 嚴綬以王師敗，乃拜弘淮西諸軍行營都統，使扞兩河，而令李光顏、烏重胤擊賊。

translations.literal: After Yan Shou's imperial army was defeated, Hong was appointed overall commander of the Huai West campaign forces, to hold the two He circuits, while Li Guangyan and Wu Chongyin were ordered to attack the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan Shou's imperial force was defeated, Hong was made overall commander of the Huai West campaign, charged with holding the two He circuits while Li Guangyan and Wu Chongyin struck at the rebels.

sentences.zh: 弘不親屯，遣子公武領兵三千屬光顏，然陰為逗橈計，以危國邀功者，每諸將告捷，輒累日不怡。

translations.literal: Hong did not personally encamp; he sent his son Gongwu leading three thousand troops under Guangyan. Yet he secretly employed delaying tactics—such as one who endangers the state to claim merit—and whenever the generals reported victories he would be displeased for days on end.
translations.idiomatic: Hong did not take the field himself, sending his son Gongwu with three thousand men to serve under Li Guangyan. Secretly he played for delay, as one who would risk the realm to claim credit, and whenever the generals reported victory he would brood for days.

sentences.zh: 元濟平，以功加兼侍中，封許國公。

translations.literal: When Yuanji was pacified, for his merit he was additionally appointed Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Yuanji was suppressed, Hong was made Palace Attendant as well and enfeoffed as Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 李師道誅，弘大懼，因請入朝，冊拜司徒、中書令，以足疾，命中人掖拜，固願留京師。

translations.literal: When Li Shidao was executed, Hong was greatly afraid; he therefore requested to come to court, was ceremonially appointed Grand Mentor and Grand Chancellor; because of foot ailment he had eunuchs support him in bowing; he firmly wished to remain in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shidao was executed, Hong was terrified and petitioned to come to court. He was ceremonially appointed Grand Mentor and Grand Chancellor; because of a foot ailment eunuchs had to support him as he bowed, and he begged to remain in the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，攝冢宰。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, he served as acting chief mourner.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, he served as acting chief mourner for the funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 俄出為河中節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as military governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was posted as military governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 以病請還，復拜司徒、中書令。

translations.literal: He requested return on grounds of illness and was again appointed Grand Mentor and Grand Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to return on grounds of illness and was again made Grand Mentor and Grand Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十八，贈太尉，謚曰隱。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-eight; posthumously given Grand Marshal, posthumous title Yin.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-eight. The court posthumously appointed him Grand Marshal and gave him the posthumous name Reticent.

sentences.zh: 始，弘自汴來朝，獻馬三千、絹五十萬、它錦彩三萬，而汴之庫廄錢尚百萬緡，絹亦百餘萬，馬七千，糧三百萬斛，兵械不可數。

translations.literal: At first when Hong came to court from Bian, he presented three thousand horses, five hundred thousand bolts of silk, and thirty thousand other brocades and silks; yet Bian's treasury and stables still had a million strings of cash, over a million bolts of silk, seven thousand horses, three million hu of grain, and weapons beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong first came to court from Bianzhou he presented three thousand horses, five hundred thousand bolts of silk, and thirty thousand pieces of brocade—yet Bian's stores still held a million strings of cash, more than a million bolts of silk, seven thousand horses, three million hu of grain, and arms beyond count.

sentences.zh: 弘為人莊重寡言，罪殺人，問法何如，不自為輕重，沈謀勇斷，故少誠、師道等皆憚之。

translations.literal: Hong as a man was solemn and taciturn; when sentencing someone to death he would ask what the law prescribed and would not decide severity himself; deep in counsel and bold in decision—therefore Shaoqian, Shidao and others all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was grave and sparing of speech. When ordering an execution he asked what the law required and never judged severity on his own. Deep in counsel and resolute in action, he was feared by men such as Shaoqian and Shidao.

sentences.zh: 詔使至，或驁侮不為禮。

translations.literal: When imperial envoys arrived, some would treat them rudely without courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial envoys arrived, he sometimes treated them with open contempt.

sentences.zh: 齊、蔡平，勢屈而後請覲，然天子尊寵異等，能以名位始終，亦其天幸。

translations.literal: Only after Qi and Cai were pacified and his power was broken did he request audience; yet the Son of Heaven honored and favored him exceptionally; that he could preserve rank and title to the end was also his heaven-sent fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Qi and Cai were pacified and his power broken did he seek an audience at court, yet the emperor honored him with extraordinary favor, and that he kept rank and title to the end was also a stroke of fortune.

sentences.zh: 子公武，字從偃。

translations.literal: His son Gongwu, courtesy name Congyan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Han Gongwu, styled Congyan.

sentences.zh: 起家衛尉主簿，為宣武行營兵馬使，以討蔡功檢校左散騎常侍、鄜坊等州節度使。

translations.literal: He began his career as registrar of the Court of Imperial Regalia, served as camp military commissioner for Xuanwu, and for merit in attacking Cai was appointed acting Left Regular Palace Attendant and military governor of Fufang and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He began as registrar in the Court of Imperial Regalia, served as Xuanwu campaign military commissioner, and for his service against Cai was made acting Left Regular Palace Attendant and military governor of Fufang and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 弘入朝，為右金吾將軍。

translations.literal: When Hong came to court, he became Right General of the Golden Quills.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Hong came to court, Gongwu was appointed Right General of the Golden Quills.

sentences.zh: 弘出河中，弘弟充徙宣武，乃曰：「二父居重鎮，我以孺子又當執金吾職乎？

translations.literal: When Hong went out to Hezhong and Hong's younger brother Chong was transferred to Xuanwu, he said: "With both father and uncle holding major commands, shall I, a mere youth, also hold the Golden Quills office?"
translations.idiomatic: When Han Hong went to Hezhong and his younger brother Chong took over Xuanwu, Gongwu said, "With my father and uncle both holding great commands, should I, still a young man, also hold a Golden Quills post?"

sentences.zh: 」因固辭，改右驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He therefore firmly declined and was changed to Grand General of the Right Majestic Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined and was reassigned as Grand General of the Right Majestic Guard.

sentences.zh: 性恭遜，不以富貴自處。

translations.literal: By nature deferential and modest, he did not comport himself as wealthy and noble.
translations.idiomatic: Modest by nature, he never acted the grandee despite his family's wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈戶部尚書，謚曰恭。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given Minister of Revenue, posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Minister of Revenue with the posthumous name Respectful.

sentences.zh: 充，本名璀，少亦依舅家。

translations.literal: Chong, original name Cui, also relied on his maternal uncle's family in youth.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, whose original name was Cui, likewise grew up in his uncle's household.

sentences.zh: 李元為河陽節度使，署牙將。

translations.literal: When Li Yuan was military governor of Heyang, he was appointed garrison officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yuan governed Heyang, he made Chong a garrison officer.

sentences.zh: 元改昭義，又從之。

translations.literal: When Yuan was transferred to Zhaoyi, he followed him again.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yuan was transferred to Zhaoyi, Chong followed him there as well.

sentences.zh: 元嘗謂賓佐曰：「充後當貴，諸君必善事之。

translations.literal: Yuan once told his staff: "Chong will later become eminent; you gentlemen must treat him well."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan once told his staff, "Chong will rise high one day. You must treat him well."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，弘領宣武，召主親兵，元曰：「我知君舊矣，吾兒不才，無足累君者，二女方幼，以為托。

translations.literal: Before long Hong took command of Xuanwu and summoned him to lead the personal guard. Yuan said: "I have known you long; my son is without talent and would not drag you down—the two daughters are still young, I entrust them to you."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Han Hong took Xuanwu and summoned Chong to lead his personal guard. Li Yuan said, "I have known you for years. My son has no talent and would not burden you; my two daughters are still young—I leave them in your care."

sentences.zh: 」遂辭去。

translations.literal: He then took his leave.
translations.idiomatic: With that he resigned and departed.

sentences.zh: 累授御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 弘峻法，人人不自保。

translations.literal: Hong had severe laws; no one felt secure.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong ruled with harsh law, and no one under him felt safe.

sentences.zh: 充謙慎無少懈，念弘在鎮久，不入見天子，身又得士，不自安，因請入宿衛，弘許之，不即遣。

translations.literal: Chong was modest and cautious without slightest slack; considering that Hong had long been at his post without entering to see the Son of Heaven, and he himself had won over soldiers, he felt ill at ease; he therefore requested to enter capital guard service. Hong agreed but did not immediately send him.
translations.idiomatic: Chong remained humble and vigilant. Knowing that Hong had long held his post without appearing at court, and that he himself had won the loyalty of the troops, he grew uneasy and asked to serve in the capital guard. Hong agreed but did not send him at once.

sentences.zh: 後因獵，單騎走洛陽，朝廷亮其節，擢右金吾衛將軍，轉大將軍，斥軍士虛名不如令者七百人。

translations.literal: Later during a hunt he rode alone to Luoyang; the court appreciated his integrity, promoted him to General of the Right Golden Quills Guard, then Grand General, and expelled seven hundred soldiers whose empty titles did not match their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during a hunt, he rode alone to Luoyang. The court respected his integrity, promoted him to General of the Right Golden Quills Guard and then Grand General, and dismissed seven hundred soldiers whose ranks did not match their actual duties.

sentences.zh: 歷少府監、鄜坊等州節度使。

translations.literal: He served successively as Director of the Palace Offices and military governor of Fufang and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Director of the Palace Offices and military governor of Fufang and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，幽、鎮、魏復亂，王承元以冀兵二千屯滑州，朝廷恐冀兵相訹為叛，徙承元鄜坊，而授充檢校尚書左仆射，為義成軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong ascended, You, Zhen, and Wei again rebelled; Wang Chengyuan stationed two thousand Ji soldiers at Huazhou; the court feared Ji troops would incite each other to rebel, transferred Chengyuan to Fufang, and appointed Chong acting Left Vice Director and military governor of Yicheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, You, Zhen, and Wei rose in rebellion again. Wang Chengyuan posted two thousand Ji troops at Huazhou; fearing they might stir one another to revolt, the court moved Chengyuan to Fufang and appointed Chong acting Left Vice Director and military governor of the Yicheng Army.

sentences.zh: 會汴軍逐李願，以李主留事。

translations.literal: At the same time Bian armies expelled Li Yuan and installed Li Zhu as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time the Bianzhou army drove out Li Yuan and installed Li Zhu as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 帝謂充素為汴士悅向，詔節度宣武，兼統義成兵討。

translations.literal: The emperor considered that Chong had long been favored by Bian soldiers; an edict made him governor of Xuanwu and jointly commanded Yicheng troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged that Chong had long enjoyed the loyalty of Bianzhou troops and ordered him to take command of Xuanwu while also leading Yicheng forces to suppress the mutiny.

sentences.zh: 戰郭橋，破之。

translations.literal: They fought at Guoqiao and broke the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At Guoqiao they fought and routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 會李質斬，遂入汴。

translations.literal: When Li Zhi was beheaded, they then entered Bian.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zhi was executed, Chong's forces entered Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，陳許李光顏亦奉詔討，屯尉氏，意先得汴，欲俘掠以餌軍，而汴監軍姚文壽亦欲內光顏。

translations.literal: At first Li Guangyan of Chen and Xu also received orders to suppress them and was encamped at Weishi; he intended to reach Bian first and wanted to capture and plunder to feed the army; meanwhile the Bian army supervisor Yao Wenshou also wished to bring Guangyan inside.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangyan of Chen and Xu had also been ordered to join the campaign and was encamped at Weishi. He hoped to reach Bianzhou first and planned to loot the city to supply his troops, while the Bianzhou army supervisor Yao Wenshou likewise wanted to bring Guangyan's force inside the city.

sentences.zh: 充聞其謀，馳至城下，汴人望見充，歡躍無復貳者。

translations.literal: Chong heard of the plot and galloped to beneath the walls; when the people of Bian saw Chong they leaped for joy and none wavered again.
translations.idiomatic: Chong learned of the plot and galloped to the city walls. When the people of Bianzhou saw him they leaped for joy, and none wavered in their loyalty again.

sentences.zh: 始，帝遣人問破賊期，充對：「汴，天下咽喉，臣頗習其人，然王師臨之，一月可破。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had sent someone to ask when the rebels would be broken; Chong replied: "Bian is the throat of the empire; I am fairly familiar with its people, yet when the imperial army comes upon it, it can be taken in a month.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had sent someone to ask when the rebels would be defeated. Chong replied, "Bianzhou is the throat of the empire. I know its people fairly well, yet when the imperial army comes upon it, the city can be taken in a month.

sentences.zh: 」方二旬即克。

translations.literal: " In barely twenty days it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: " In barely twenty days it fell.

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「充料敵若神。

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure: "Chong gauges the enemy like a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with pleasure, "Chong gauges the enemy like a god.

sentences.zh: 」加檢校司空。

translations.literal: " He was advanced to acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: " He was advanced to acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 籍所脅為兵者三萬，悉縱之。

translations.literal: Of those registered as conscripted soldiers there were thirty thousand; he released them all.
translations.idiomatic: Of the thirty thousand men who had been conscripted by force, he released them all.

sentences.zh: 又責首亂者千餘，斥出境，令曰：「敢後者斬！

translations.literal: He also held accountable more than a thousand ringleaders of the disorder, expelled them beyond the borders, and proclaimed: "Whoever dares linger shall be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: He also held accountable more than a thousand ringleaders of the mutiny, expelled them beyond the borders, and proclaimed, "Whoever dares linger shall be beheaded!

sentences.zh: 」由是內外按堵，汴人愛賴之。

translations.literal: " Thereby within and without were settled in peace, and the people of Bian came to love and rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereafter the city was settled within and without, and the people of Bianzhou came to love and rely on him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十五，贈司徒，謚曰肅。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-five; he was posthumously made Grand Mentor and given the posthumous title Su, "Solemn."
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-five. He was posthumously made Grand Mentor and given the posthumous title Su, "Solemn."

sentences.zh: 充雖將家，性儉節，歷三鎮，居處服玩如儒先生，乘機決策無余悔，世推善將。

translations.literal: Although Chong came from a general's family, by nature he was frugal and restrained; through three commands his dwelling, dress, and furnishings were like a Confucian scholar's; seizing opportunity in decision he left no regrets, and the age acclaimed him a fine commander.
translations.idiomatic: Although Chong came from a general's family, he was by nature frugal and restrained. Through three commands his dwelling, dress, and furnishings were those of a Confucian scholar. He seized opportunity in decision and left no regrets, and his age acclaimed him a fine commander.

sentences.zh: 李元沒，充為嫁二女，周其家。

translations.literal: When Li Yuan died, Chong married off his two daughters and supported his household.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yuan died, Chong married off his two daughters and supported his household.

sentences.zh: 自弘去汴，監軍選軍中敢士二千直閣下，日秩酒肴，物力幾屈，然不敢廢。

translations.literal: Since Hong had left Bian, the army supervisor selected two thousand bold soldiers from the army to stand guard below the pavilion; daily rations of wine and food were issued, and material resources were nearly exhausted, yet they did not dare abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han Hong had left Bianzhou, the army supervisor selected two thousand bold soldiers from the army to stand guard below the pavilion. Daily rations of wine and food were issued, and material resources were nearly exhausted, yet no one dared abolish the practice.

sentences.zh: 充未入時，李質總軍事，乃曰：「韓公至而頓去二千人食，豈不失人心乎？

translations.literal: Before Chong had entered, Li Zhi was in overall charge of military affairs; he said: "When Lord Han arrives and suddenly cuts off food for two thousand men, will that not lose the hearts of the people?
translations.idiomatic: Before Chong had entered the city, Li Zhi was in overall charge of military affairs. He said, "When Lord Han arrives and suddenly cuts off food for two thousand men, will that not lose the hearts of the troops?

sentences.zh: 不去，且無以繼，可以弊事遺吾帥乎！

translations.literal: If they are not removed, there will be no means to continue it—can a ruinous affair be left to our commander!
translations.idiomatic: If they are not removed, there will be no means to sustain it. Can we leave a ruinous burden for our commander to inherit!

sentences.zh: 」因悉罷之而後迎充。

translations.literal: " He therefore abolished them entirely and only then welcomed Chong.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore abolished the practice entirely and only then welcomed Chong.

sentences.zh: 李質者，節士也。

translations.literal: Li Zhi was a man of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi was a man of integrity.

sentences.zh: 始為牙將，及為留後，邀帥節，勸之不從。

translations.literal: He had begun as a guard officer; when he became acting commander he invited the commander's banner and staff, but when he urged acceptance Zhi would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He had begun as a guard officer. When he became acting commander he invited the commander's banner and staff, but when he urged acceptance Li Zhi would not listen.

sentences.zh: 疽發於首，委質以兵，遂禽。

translations.literal: When a carbuncle broke out on his head he entrusted his person and troops to Zhi, who thereupon captured him.
translations.idiomatic: When a carbuncle broke out on his head he entrusted his person and troops to Li Zhi, who thereupon captured him.

sentences.zh: 終金吾將軍。

translations.literal: He ended as general of the Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as general of the Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：臯、建封、弘本諸生，震興田畝間，未有以異人，及投隙龍驤，皆為國梁楹，光奮一時。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Gao, Jianfeng, and Hong were originally scholars; Zhen rose from the fields—none was marked out as extraordinary men, yet when they seized their openings and soared like dragons they all became pillars of the state, shining brilliantly for a time.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Gao, Jianfeng, and Hong were originally scholars; Zhen rose from the fields. None was marked out in advance as extraordinary, yet when they seized their openings and soared like dragons they all became pillars of the state, shining brilliantly for a time.

sentences.zh: 使不遭遇，與庸夫汩汩並胔而腐可也。

translations.literal: Had they not met with opportunity, they might have rotted away with common men in the common stream, corpses piled together.
translations.idiomatic: Had they not met with opportunity, they might have rotted away with common men in the common stream, corpses piled together.

sentences.zh: 臯、弘雖陰慝，卒能以誠言自解，長沒天年，宜哉！

translations.literal: Gao and Hong, though secretly malicious, were still able in the end to clear themselves with sincere words and live out their natural span—fitting indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Gao and Hong, though secretly malicious, were still able in the end to clear themselves with sincere words and live out their natural span. Fitting indeed!
